Founded in 2018 and headquartered in New York, NY, Talos unifies an order/execution management system (OEMS), a portfolio management system (PMS), and institutional market data on a single platform — covering price discovery, execution, portfolio construction, risk management, treasury, and settlement. Institutions such as hedge funds, banks, broker-dealers, asset managers, ETF issuers, and neobanks reach global liquidity through the Talos Network of 100+ providers (exchanges, OTC desks, prime brokers, custodians, DeFi protocols, and FX providers) and connect programmatically over FIX, REST, and WebSocket APIs. Developer documentation is gated behind client authentication (Auth0); this profile was enriched from Talos's public surface (llms.txt, GitHub org, and trust center).

providers.name: Chainflip
providers.description: Chainflip is a decentralised, permissionless cross-chain protocol for native asset swaps and cross-chain lending. It lets users and integrators swap and borrow against native assets such as BTC, ETH, SOL, USDC, USDT, TRX, and DOT across chains without wrapped assets, traditional bridges, or centralised custody. The protocol runs as a Proof-of-Stake MPC network of roughly 150 validators securing a fully on-chain trading system built on an application-specific State Chain and a just-in-time (JIT) AMM liquidity design. Developers integrate via the typed @chainflip/sdk JavaScript SDK and the Broker / State Chain JSON-RPC interfaces to fetch quotes, request deposit addresses, encode vault swaps, and route swaps for broker commission.

providers.name: HashKey Cloud (HashQuark)
providers.description: HashKey Cloud, formerly HashQuark, is a Hong Kong-based blockchain infrastructure and Web3 staking provider (part of HashKey Group) that runs enterprise-grade validator nodes across 50+ mainstream proof-of-stake public chains including Ethereum, Cosmos, Solana, Polkadot, Avalanche, Sui and BNB Chain. It exposes a developer platform for institutional staking: a Staking API to onboard users, generate deposits, assign and exit validators and drive pooled staking; a Data API to track node status and daily/monthly/quarterly/ annual reward data; plus a dashboard, a Babylon BTC staking flow and a first-party Go SDK. Requests are authenticated with a custom Quark-Keccak256-ECDSA request-signing scheme keyed to an Ethereum keypair. Originally added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub (surfaced via Qiming), now enriched from HashKey Cloud's public developer surface.

providers.name: Discover Financial Services
providers.description: Discover Financial Services is a US direct bank and payments company that owns the Discover Network, the PULSE debit network, and Diners Club International. Its Discover Global Network (DGN) developer program exposes a partner-gated developer center with interactive OpenAPI documentation for card-network products — EMV 3-D Secure (ProtectBuy), Secure Remote Commerce / Click to Pay, Stored Token Services (tokenization), and Discover Deliver push payments. Consumer account-data access is delivered through open-finance aggregators (Plaid, Finicity) rather than a first-party retail-banking API.

providers.name: Bittensor
providers.description: Bittensor is an open, decentralized machine-intelligence network built on a Substrate blockchain (subtensor). Contributors earn the TAO token by supplying useful work to specialized subnets — miners produce, validators score, and stakers back them — with emissions distributed by Yuma Consensus. Developers do not consume a hosted REST API; they interact with the chain through the official lean Python SDK (import bittensor) and the btcli command line, which together perform every user-facing operation: wallets and keys, staking and pools, subnet creation, mining, validating, weights, proxies, multisig, and an EVM layer. The developer surface is agent-native: machine-readable catalogs of write intents, chain reads, and errors are published for discovery, with a plan/execute model, Policy guardrails, and typed results.

providers.name: CipherTrust
providers.description: CipherTrust Manager is Thales's centralized key- and data-security management platform and the control plane of the CipherTrust Data Security Platform (CDSP). It provides a unified plane for encryption key lifecycle management, secrets management, certificates, tokenization, data discovery, and policy enforcement across on-premises, hybrid, and multi-cloud environments including AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud, with HSM/KMIP integration, Kubernetes and DevSecOps support, role-based access controls, and post-quantum cryptography readiness. Developers and platform teams automate it through a REST API (base path /api/v1, JWT bearer authentication), an official HashiCorp Terraform provider (ThalesGroup/ciphertrust), an Ansible collection, and PowerShell orchestration modules, plus Application Protection SDKs for embedding encryption, key management, and tokenization in apps.

providers.name: Offchain Labs
providers.description: Offchain Labs (now operating as "Offchain") is the research-and-engineering company behind Arbitrum, one of the leading Ethereum Layer 2 scaling ecosystems, and Prysm, an Ethereum consensus client that powers a large share of the network. Its technology stack includes Arbitrum Nitro (the rollup node software), Arbitrum Stylus (a framework for writing smart contracts in Rust, C, and C++ compiled to WebAssembly), the Arbitrum Orbit / Arbitrum chains SDK for launching app-specific chains, and BoLD for permissionless dispute resolution. For developers the surface is Ethereum JSON-RPC endpoints for Arbitrum One, Nova, and Sepolia, plus first-party TypeScript, Rust, Go, and Solidity SDKs, the cargo-stylus CLI, and extensive documentation at docs.arbitrum.io.

providers.name: Gensyn
providers.description: Gensyn is a decentralized infrastructure company building "the network for machine intelligence" — protocols that let AI systems train, verify, and transact in market-driven ecosystems. Its stack includes AXL (peer-to-peer networking for ML nodes, with built-in MCP/A2A support), CHAIN (on-chain identity, reputation, and stake), and REE (the Reproducible Execution Environment for cryptographically verifiable ML compute). Its flagship application, Delphi, is a live on-chain information (prediction) market where humans and AI agents trade predictions with on-chain settlement. Gensyn publishes a TypeScript Delphi SDK and an agent-skills package so autonomous agents can discover markets, quote, trade, and redeem positions programmatically. Backed by a16z.

providers.name: DFINITY
providers.description: The DFINITY Foundation is a Swiss-based not-for-profit research organization that created and stewards the Internet Computer Protocol (ICP), a public, decentralized "frontier cloud" that hosts software and data entirely inside a mathematical network protocol. Applications run as canisters (WebAssembly smart contracts with persistent state, native HTTP, and a reverse gas model paid in Cycles) that are tamperproof, unstoppable, and free from vendor lock-in. ICP uses Chain Key cryptography and Chain Fusion to transact natively on Bitcoin and Ethereum without bridges, and is governed on-network by the Network Nervous System (NNS). DFINITY publishes first-party developer tooling — JavaScript/TypeScript agent libraries under the @dfinity npm scope, Rust agent and Canister Developer Kit crates, the icp/dfx CLIs, and an AI agent skills library — plus a public HTTP interface for reading from and calling canisters.

providers.name: Sorella Labs
providers.description: Sorella Labs is a crypto-infrastructure company building Angstrom, a new kind of decentralized exchange (DEX) built on top of Uniswap V4 that internalizes MEV through application-level sequencing. By enforcing its own transaction ordering, Angstrom redirects value that would normally be extracted by MEV bots and validators back to the actual participants — liquidity providers and swappers. The company also builds Brontes, a Rust blockchain-analytics engine specialized in systematic MEV detection. Angstrom exposes a decentralized JSON-RPC API — each node runs its own JSON-RPC server, with a recommended load-balanced HTTPS/WebSocket endpoint plus a separate on-chain Data API — and ships Rust libraries (angstrom-sdk, angstrom-v4) for integrators, routers, and solvers. Backed by Paradigm.

providers.name: Manta Network
providers.description: Manta Network is a modular Layer-2 blockchain ecosystem for zero-knowledge (ZK) applications, comprising two complementary networks. Manta Pacific is an EVM-compatible Ethereum Layer-2 rollup built on the Optimism OP Stack that uses Celestia for modular data availability, giving developers low-gas deployment of ZK applications through the standard Ethereum JSON-RPC interface (chain ID 169). Manta Atlantic is a Polkadot parachain (Para ID 2104) focused on on-chain ZK identity and privacy, exposed through Substrate/Polkadot JSON-RPC over WebSocket. Developers build with familiar EVM tooling, deploy against a public Sepolia testnet and faucet, and interact with the network via public RPC endpoints, block explorers, and native bridges. Manta Network is backed by Polychain Capital and other investors.

providers.name: dYdX
providers.description: Decentralized cryptocurrency exchange

providers.name: Element
providers.description: Element (Element Finance) is an Andreessen Horowitz-backed decentralized finance protocol for fixed and variable yield on crypto assets. The protocol splits an interest-bearing position into tradable Principal Tokens (PTs) and Yield Tokens (YTs) so users can lock in a fixed rate by buying discounted principal, or take variable-rate exposure, redeeming at face value on maturity via on-chain AMMs. It also ships the Council governance framework (voting vaults, delegation, the Governance Steering Council) that powers the Element DAO. Element is a smart-contract protocol on Ethereum rather than a hosted REST API: developers integrate through the on-chain contracts, the elf-sdk TypeScript library, and the published contract reference. The team has since rebranded to DELV (delvtech).

providers.name: Unchained Capital
providers.description: Unchained (Unchained Capital, Inc.) is an Austin, Texas bitcoin-native financial services company built around collaborative multisig custody. Clients hold bitcoin in 2-of-3 multisig vaults where the client holds two keys and Unchained holds one, so no single party — including Unchained — can move funds unilaterally, and clients can recover independently with open-source tooling such as Caravan and Sparrow. On top of that custody base Unchained offers a trading desk for buying and selling bitcoin directly to cold storage, bitcoin-backed loans, the Unchained IRA (Traditional, Roth, SEP and 401(k) rollovers), business and trust vaults, inheritance planning, and — through Gannett Trust and Gannett Wealth Advisors — fiduciary trust and wealth advisory services. Unchained publishes no public REST or GraphQL API; its public developer surface is a set of open-source bitcoin libraries (unchained-bitcoin, unchained-wallets, hermit, and the Caravan multisig coordinator, now maintained in the caravan-bitcoin organization) plus an llms.txt for AI agents.

providers.name: dClimate
providers.description: dClimate is a chain-agnostic, decentralized climate information ecosystem that makes it easy for businesses, governments, and builders to find, access, and utilize essential data about the planet. Rather than a conventional REST API, dClimate exposes its weather and climate data SDK-first over content-addressed (IPFS/IPLD) storage: official Python and JavaScript clients resolve datasets from a STAC catalog and stream sharded Zarr stores, requiring no API key or OAuth for public data. Offerings span weather/climate reanalysis and forecast sources such as ECMWF ERA5 and AIFS, a Data Marketplace featuring datasets from providers like NASA and ESA, plus the Aegis and CYCLOPS climate-intelligence platforms. Backed by Multicoin Capital.

providers.name: Rocket Pool
providers.description: Rocket Pool is a decentralized Ethereum liquid staking protocol that lets anyone participate in Ethereum proof-of-stake without running a full 32 ETH validator. Stakers deposit ETH and receive rETH, a rebasing-free yield-bearing liquid staking token that automatically accrues consensus and execution layer rewards and is freely composable across DeFi. On the supply side, permissionless node operators can run a Rocket Pool minipool with as little as 8 ETH (and a smaller RPL bond) — Rocket Pool pairs operator ETH with the rETH-backed deposit pool to fund full beacon-chain validators, and operators earn consensus rewards plus a commission from rETH users and RPL inflation rewards. The protocol is governed on-chain through the Protocol DAO (pDAO) and the Oracle DAO (oDAO) and is specified by Rocket Pool Improvement Proposals (RPIPs). The reference node software stack is the Smart Node (rocketpool CLI plus a Go daemon) distributed as Docker images, alongside Go and TypeScript/JavaScript libraries (rocketpool-go, rocketpool-js) for reading and writing protocol state directly against the Rocket Pool smart contracts on Ethereum mainnet. Rocket Pool has no centralized REST API, no hosted developer platform, no API keys, and no pricing — all participation is on-chain via Ethereum JSON-RPC and the protocol's deployed contracts.

providers.name: Blockstream
providers.description: Blockstream is a Bitcoin infrastructure company whose products include the Liquid Network sidechain, the Green self-custody wallet, Blockstream Satellite, and Bitcoin mining and data services. For developers its flagship public API is Esplora, the open-source Bitcoin block explorer behind blockstream.info: a no-authentication HTTP REST API for reading blocks, transactions, addresses, scripthashes, the mempool, and fee estimates across Bitcoin mainnet, testnet, and signet, plus Liquid/Elements issued assets. Amounts are returned in satoshis and hashes are hex-encoded, with cursor pagination over confirmed transaction history. Blockstream also ships GDK, its open-source cross-platform wallet SDK.

providers.name: Bitmex
providers.description: Real-Time Cryptocurrency derivatives trading platform based in Hong Kong

providers.name: Chronicled
providers.description: Chronicled is a San Francisco technology company that builds and administers the blockchain-powered MediLedger Network, a decentralized platform that automates business-rule enforcement and trusted data exchange between trading partners in the pharmaceutical and life sciences supply chain. Its solutions span DSCSA-compliant product verification, contracts and chargebacks, gross-to-net (GPO roster and rebate) reconciliation, and customer master data management for manufacturers, wholesalers, distributors, health systems, and group purchasing organizations. Chronicled publishes no public API, developer portal, or OpenAPI; it operates a private B2B network and is backed by Pantera Capital.

providers.name: Community Labs
providers.description: Community Labs is an independent research organization founded in 2022 by Tate Berenbaum, oriented toward a single belief: access to the future of intelligence should not be gate kept by the hardware people can afford. The company raised a $30M seed round led by Lightspeed Venture Partners, originally operating as a native software development company and venture studio accelerating developer tools and adoption of the Arweave permaweb, and has since refocused on local and consumer-hardware AI inference research. Its open source surface spans Hypura, a storage-tier-aware LLM inference scheduler for Apple Silicon that exposes an Ollama-compatible HTTP API, Autolab, an autonomous research orchestration framework, and the labscommunity GitHub organization of Arweave developer libraries including ArweaveKit, Arweave Wallet Kit, and the Arweave Storage SDK.

providers.name: Kyash
providers.description: Kyash Inc. (株式会社Kyash) is a Tokyo-based fintech founded in 2015 that operates a consumer mobile wallet and Visa prepaid card in Japan, covering charging, peer-to-peer transfers, shared accounts, buy-now-pay-later, personal finance management, and contactless payment through Apple Pay, Google Pay, and Samsung Pay. Kyash is a registered Funds Transfer Service Provider (Kanto Local Finance Bureau No. 00082) and a third-party Prepaid Payment Instrument Issuer (No. 00698), and is ISO/IEC 27001:2022, PCI DSS, and TRUSTe certified. Its business-facing product is Kyash Payout, a mass payout service that sends funds to Japanese domestic bank accounts or Kyash wallets at a flat 50 yen per transfer, integrated either by Zengin/CSV file upload or by direct API integration including a balance API. Kyash previously sold Kyash Direct, an API-based Visa card issuer processing platform launched in 2019. All API access is sales-gated: Kyash publishes no developer portal, API reference, specification, SDK, or sandbox.

providers.name: American Express
providers.description: American Express is a globally integrated payments company and card network that offers charge and credit cards, merchant acquiring, corporate payments, travel, and Membership Rewards loyalty. Its developer platform at developer.americanexpress.com publishes a partner-oriented catalog of REST APIs spanning tokenization (AETS), fraud prevention (Enhanced Authorization), PSD2 open-banking account, transaction and confirmation-of-funds services, corporate @ Work expense management, Pay with Points redemption, Pay with Bank transfer payment initiation, Payment Account Reference, card-linked Smart Offers, Account Connect card-on-file, and the R42 Network Loyalty Platform. Access is onboarding-gated for registered issuers, merchants, acquirers, and partners rather than open self-service.

providers.name: Dash
providers.description: Dash is a peer-to-peer cryptocurrency network offering fast, low-cost payments with InstantSend, privacy via CoinJoin mixing, and decentralized governance through Masternodes. Developers can query blocks, transactions, addresses, UTXOs, governance objects, and real-time network events through the open-source Insight REST and WebSocket API, and can access Dash Platform layer-2 (DashPay identity, data contracts, documents, tokens) through the Decentralized API (DAPI) over gRPC and JSON-RPC.

providers.name: Lens Protocol
providers.description: Lens Protocol is an onchain social graph and a developer platform for building social applications where users own their profile, content, and relationships. Originally launched on Polygon PoS, Lens has since evolved into Lens Chain — an L2 zkEVM rollup purpose-built for social — with the Lens v3 contracts redesigned around primitives like Accounts, Apps, Feeds, Groups, Graphs, and Actions. Developers integrate Lens through the Lens API (a GraphQL gateway over the indexed chain state), the Lens TypeScript SDK and React SDK, the underlying smart contracts, and an authentication layer that issues short-lived auth tokens after a SIWE-style signature. Lens powers social clients (Hey, Orb, Tape, Buttrfly), creator tools, and composable mini-apps that share the same onchain social graph.

providers.name: Superfluid
providers.description: Superfluid is a money-streaming protocol for real-time, on-chain cashflows, enabling continuous "payments by the second" to any wallet address across EVM networks. Built by Superfluid Labs, the protocol powers salaries, subscriptions, rewards, airdrops, vesting, and incentive distributions as programmable token streams and distribution pools. Developers integrate via first-party TypeScript SDKs (@superfluid-finance/sdk-core, sdk-redux), the on-chain smart contracts (@superfluid-finance/ethereum-contracts), an embeddable checkout Widget, and a public GraphQL Subgraph API served through The Graph for querying streams, pools, accounts, and token statistics. The protocol has streamed over $1.6B to 1.27M recipients across DeFi, SocialFi, and gaming use cases.

providers.name: BNY Mellon
providers.description: BNY Mellon (legal parent The Bank of New York Mellon Corporation, rebranded to "BNY" in 2024) is a US money-center bank and the world's largest custodian, overseeing roughly $50 trillion in assets under custody and/or administration. Its principal banking subsidiary, The Bank of New York Mellon, is a nationally chartered bank (OCC-supervised) headquartered in New York City, operating across Securities Services, Market & Wealth Services, and Investment & Wealth Management with brand families including Pershing, Eagle Investment Systems, and BNY Markets. On open finance, BNY runs a genuine first-party developer program — the BNY Developer Marketplace at developer.bny.com (formerly marketplace.bnymellon.com) — publishing Treasury Services (payments, liquidity, cash management, trade finance, FX), Asset Servicing, Markets, and Pershing API families to corporate, fintech, and financial-institution clients. Registration and full API reference are gated behind Nexen single sign-on, and no OpenAPI/Swagger is publicly downloadable. BNY also ships a public, smart-contract-only "Data On-Chain" product that broadcasts fund accounting data to Ethereum. Consumer/business-banking account data is reached primarily through aggregators such as Plaid rather than a first-party consumer data API. No FDX participation or CFPB 1033 posture is publicly documented.

providers.name: Coinbase Pro
providers.description: Cryptocurrency Trading Platform

providers.name: Xapo
providers.description: Xapo Bank is a members-only private bank and Bitcoin custodian founded in 2013, combining regulated fiat banking with institutional-grade Bitcoin custody in a single app. Members earn interest on Bitcoin and USD balances, borrow against Bitcoin without selling, invest in US stocks and ETFs, and transact globally in multiple currencies. Xapo Bank Limited is regulated by the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission as a credit institution (Permission No. 23171), with Xapo VASP Limited licensed as a DLT Provider (Permission No. 26061). The company publishes SOC 2 Type II / SOC 3, PCI DSS, and GDPR compliance claims but operates app-only today, with no public developer API or portal; legacy Xapo Bitcoin API SDKs remain on PyPI and RubyGems from its pre-bank wallet era.

providers.name: CoinDCX
providers.description: Cryptocurrency Trading Platform

providers.name: Huobi
providers.description: Seychelles based cryptocurrency exchange

providers.name: Parsec Finance
providers.description: Parsec Finance is an institutional-grade on-chain analytics platform for DeFi and NFT markets. Its modular "Command Center" lets traders and analysts drag and drop dozens of real-time components — live trade firehoses, liquidity-depth charts, wallet trackers, lending dashboards and NFT floor monitors — across many EVM chains. Beyond the app, Parsec exposes a Pro GraphQL API at api.parsec.finance for programmatic access to on-chain market data: DEX trades, OHLCV candles, lending markets, liquidity pools (including concentrated-liquidity positions), NFT collections and trades, token holders and balance changes, transfers, transactions, contract logs, trending contracts, trade metrics and address label resolution. A first-party Python SDK (parsecfi) wraps the API. Parsec is used by firms such as Polychain and Galaxy Digital.

providers.name: Ramper
providers.description: Ramper is a Web3 embedded-wallet and social-login platform that lets DApps onboard users with familiar Web2 credentials (Email, Google, Facebook, Apple, Twitter) and instantly create non-custodial, self-custody wallets with no seed phrases, browser extensions, or downloads. Its Embedded Wallet SDK ships as first-party npm packages for web (@ramper-v2/core, @ramper-v2/multi, @ramper/ethereum, @ramper/near, @ramper/terra, @ramper/chiliz, @ramper/viction), React Native mobile, Unity, and Telegram Mini Apps, and is compatible with ethers.js across EVM chains plus NEAR, Solana, BNB Chain, Sei, and Viction. Ramper also provides an embeddable WalletView (balances, transfers, transaction signing, fiat on-ramp) and a fiat NFT Checkout SDK. Developers integrate via an App ID / App Secret issued from the Developer Dashboard.

providers.name: KGeN
providers.description: KGeN (Kratos Gamer Network) is a verified-human data network powering Physical AI and Large Language Models across the Global South, and the operator of the KGeN Economy Protocols — a suite of developer APIs (Esports and Loyalty) that let game studios add leaderboard-based competitions and customizable reward systems paid in KCash, redeemable for real-world items at the Kratos Store. Server-to-server and per-user (JWT/OTP) endpoints cover sessions, tournaments, wallets, rewards, and rewardable events. Company revenue feeds $KGEN tokenomics, where every AI-data contract permanently retires token supply on-chain. Backed by Accel and Prosus Ventures.

providers.name: Offchain Labs (Arbitrum)
providers.description: Offchain Labs is the team behind Arbitrum, a suite of Ethereum Layer 2 scaling technologies (Arbitrum One and Arbitrum Nova) built on the Nitro tech stack and the AnyTrust and Rollup protocols. Rather than a traditional REST API, Arbitrum exposes an Ethereum-compatible JSON-RPC interface plus Arbitrum-specific precompiles and the NodeInterface, and ships first-party developer tooling: the TypeScript Arbitrum SDK for bridging and cross-chain messaging, the Orbit SDK for launching custom Arbitrum chains, and the Stylus SDK (Rust/Wasm) with the cargo-stylus CLI for writing EVM-compatible smart contracts. This profile was seeded as a pantera-capital portfolio lead and enriched from Arbitrum's public developer surface.

providers.name: Reflexer
providers.description: Reflexer Labs builds RAI, a decentralized, non-pegged stable asset backed by ETH on Ethereum. Rather than tracking the US dollar, RAI uses an on-chain PID controller and algorithmic redemption rate to achieve relative price stability. The protocol is built on GEB, Reflexer's open-source framework of smart contracts for SAFEs (collateralized debt positions), liquidations, auctions, oracles, and governance minimization. Developers integrate via the geb.js (JavaScript/TypeScript) and pyflex (Python) SDKs and query protocol state through a hosted GraphQL subgraph (The Graph Protocol). Sector: crypto / DeFi stablecoins.

providers.name: Wealthsimple
providers.description: Wealthsimple is a Toronto-based Canadian financial technology company, founded in 2014, offering a full suite of consumer financial products: managed investing (Invest), self-directed stock and ETF trading (Trade), cryptocurrency, tax filing (Tax), spending, saving, and cash and card products. It serves more than four million Canadians with roughly CAD $125 billion in assets under administration and reached a CAD $10 billion valuation in its 2025 Series F round. Wealthsimple does not publish an official public developer API or OpenAPI specification; programmatic account access is available only through open-banking aggregators (SnapTrade, Plaid) and community-built unofficial libraries. This profile captures the company's public trust, security, and developer-adjacent surface (security.txt, HackerOne bug bounty, Trust Center, status page, verified GitHub organization).

providers.name: Ronin Network
providers.description: Ronin is an Ethereum sidechain originally built by Sky Mavis to power Axie Infinity and a wider game and NFT economy. The network exposes a standard Ethereum-style JSON-RPC interface on mainnet and the Saigon testnet, the Ronin Explorer, a canonical bridge to Ethereum, and the Skynet Web3 data API for indexed accounts, NFTs, contracts, and transactions. Sky Mavis layers on game and platform APIs (Axie Infinity Origins, AXP, Ronin Market Partner, Ronin Store, Account, Wallet, Gas Sponsoring, Katana Swap) administered through the Ronin Developer Console.

providers.name: Sender
providers.description: Sender (Sender Wallet, by Sender Labs / SENDER TECH LIMITED) is a self-custody multi-chain Web3 wallet for NEAR, Ethereum and all EVM-compatible chains (Polygon, BNB Chain, Arbitrum, Optimism, Avalanche, Scroll, zkSync Era, TON and 20+ networks), shipping as a Chrome/Brave/Edge browser extension and iOS and Android apps. For developers, Sender exposes an injected browser-provider API: dApps detect the wallet on window.sender.near / window.sender.ethereum (with legacy window.near support), request sign-in / account access, and sign and broadcast transactions. The Ethereum provider follows EIP-1193 and EIP-1102; NEAR exposes requestSignIn, signAndSendTransaction and request. The wallet is audited by SlowMist and runs a bug bounty. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Pantera Capital.

providers.name: Spheron
providers.description: Spheron Network is a decentralized GPU and cloud compute marketplace that aggregates enterprise-grade NVIDIA GPU capacity from certified Tier 3/4 data centers worldwide and exposes it through a single on-demand, per-minute billed interface. The marketplace covers H100, H200, B200, B300, A100, GH200, L40S, RTX PRO 6000, RTX 5090, RTX 4090, and pre-order GB200/GB300/ R100 inventory, priced 40-60% below hyperscaler rates with spot, reserved, and custom-cluster (8-512+ GPU) options. Teams access the platform through a web dashboard, a documented REST API at app.spheron.ai/api, a TypeScript Protocol SDK, an MCP plugin for Claude, SkyPilot integration, and Helm charts for self-hosted provider nodes. The Spheron Foundation also maintains an open compute protocol with Fizz nodes, provider nodes, ICL YAML configuration, and an on-chain payment system supporting both traditional payment rails and USDC/USDT stablecoin settlement. The company is transitioning from a pure decentralized protocol model toward an enterprise GPU procurement and aggregation marketplace while keeping the underlying provider network open and community-operated.

providers.name: 3Jane
providers.description: 3Jane is an Ethereum-mainnet credit-based money market that issues algorithmic, real-time uncollateralized USDC credit lines underwritten against verifiable financial proofs rather than on-chain collateral. Its 3CA credit-assessment algorithm and Jane Score combine on-chain history with off-chain signals (bank data via Plaid, VantageScore/credit metadata, zkTLS proofs via Reclaim Protocol and EigenLayer). Capital suppliers deposit USDC to mint USD3, a yieldcoin with a senior claim on interest repayments, or stake it for sUSD3, a junior tranche that earns levered yield while absorbing first losses. Backing comes from Fintech Credit Conduits (warehouse loans and forward-flow programs for U.S. fintech lenders) and Crypto Credit Lines. The protocol is governed by a timelock and multisig and coordinated by the JANE token. 3Jane raised a $5.2M seed round led by Paradigm, with Coinbase Ventures and Wintermute Ventures participating.

providers.name: Acala
providers.description: Acala is the decentralized finance (DeFi) and liquidity hub of the Polkadot ecosystem, operating the Acala parachain (and its Kusama-based sister network Karura). Acala offers a scalable, Ethereum-compatible smart-contract platform called Acala EVM+, a decentralized stablecoin (aUSD), a liquid staking derivative (LDOT/LcDOT), and a trustless staking and swap layer. For developers, Acala EVM+ exposes a standard Ethereum JSON-RPC interface through its EVM+ RPC Adapter (eth-rpc-adapter), letting existing Ethereum dApps, wallets (MetaMask), and tooling (Hardhat, Remix, ethers.js, Truffle) interact with the Substrate-based chain with minimal changes, alongside a Substrate WebSocket RPC via the @acala-network Polkadot.js API and SDK packages.

providers.name: Level
providers.description: Level is a stablecoin protocol that issued lvlUSD, a stablecoin fully backed by USDC and USDT which were deployed into blue-chip lending protocols (Aave and the Morpho Steakhouse USDC vault) to generate yield. Lending yield was passed back to holders through an ERC-4626 staking mechanism: lvlUSD could be staked for slvlUSD, a yield-accruing token that appreciates as the protocol distributes yield into the staking contract. Both tokens were transferable and integrated across DeFi venues including Morpho, Pendle, Spectra and Curve, with LayerZero OFT adapters bridging them to Base. Level exposes no public HTTP API — its programmable surface is a set of audited Ethereum mainnet smart contracts (lvlUSD, slvlUSD, LevelMinting, LevelStakingPool, LevelUsdPointsFarm, LevelReserveLens) documented in GitBook and published on GitHub. In September 2025 the team announced it was joining the Sky (fka MakerDAO) ecosystem as part of Grove and that the Level protocol is being sunset: mints paused, redemptions made public and fixed 1:1, cooldowns cut to two seconds, final yield distribution on 2025-10-02, and the front end retired on 2025-12-15 with contract-level redemption remaining available indefinitely.

providers.name: Agoric
providers.description: Agoric is a Cosmos-based Layer 1 blockchain that lets developers build secure cross-chain smart contracts in Hardened JavaScript (SES). Its Orchestration API abstracts multiple chains so a single long-lived contract can manage assets, accounts, and services across the multi-chain universe. The platform is built around Zoe (a smart-contract framework that enforces offer safety), ERTP (the Electronic Rights Transfer Protocol for issuing and transferring digital assets), and SwingSet (its deterministic async VM). Developers ship dapps with the `agoric` CLI and `agd` Cosmos daemon, query chain state through vstorage, and integrate with the network over Cosmos RPC and IBC. The developer surface is delivered as first-party `@agoric/*` npm packages rather than a REST API. Originally surfaced as a Polychain portfolio company, this profile has been enriched from Agoric's public developer platform.

providers.name: Globacap
providers.description: Globacap is a London-based private capital markets technology company, founded in 2017, that builds workflow-automation software-as-a-service for issuance, share register management, ongoing administration, transferability and settlement of private securities. Its platform is used by securities exchanges, securities firms, private banks and asset managers to run primary placements and secondary liquidity events, and the company states its technology has supported 200+ primary placements, matched and settled $800m+ of secondaries and administered $30bn+ in private markets assets. Globacap operates an FCA-regulated UK entity and a US-registered broker-dealer and alternative trading system. In November 2025 Apex Group agreed to acquire the company; the change of control completed in early 2026 and Globacap technology now sits inside Apex Group's digital/tokenisation initiative alongside Tokeny. As of this profile the public globacap.com site has been reduced to a single acquisition announcement page and Globacap publishes no public developer program, API reference or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Finary
providers.description: Finary is a French fintech platform for personal wealth tracking and management that aggregates a user's entire net worth — stocks, funds, ETFs, cryptocurrency, real estate, savings, life insurance, startups and other alternative assets — into a single dashboard by connecting to 20,000+ banks and brokers worldwide. Beyond tracking, Finary offers fee detection, diversification and sector/geo allocation analysis, dividend monitoring, budgeting, in-app crypto buying/selling and staking, and life-insurance products. The company reports more than one million users and is regulated in France by the AMF and ACPR. Finary does not publish an official public REST API or SDKs; the app frontends talk to a private API that the developer community has reverse-engineered into an unofficial OpenAPI spec and language wrappers.

providers.name: Hamsa
providers.description: Hamsa (formerly HamsaPay) is a San Francisco-based financial infrastructure company "powering the Finternet." It builds the Hamsa Unified Confidential Ledger (UCL), a privacy-enabled, EVM-compatible, permissioned Layer-2 blockchain for banks and financial institutions, plus the Hamsa Privacy module that uses zero-knowledge-proof (ZKP) rollups on Hyperledger Besu to run confidential Delivery-versus-Payment (DvP) and Payment-versus-Payment (PvP) settlement, tokenized deposits, stablecoins, and CBDCs. The developer platform exposes an EVM-standard JSON-RPC API (eth_* methods) and DvP escrow smart contracts, authenticated with Ethereum message signatures and role-based access control. Hamsa has tokenized over $3.2B for Tier-1/Tier-2 banks (including Banco Safra's Safra Dolar stablecoin) and participates in the Brazilian Drex CBDC pilot.

providers.name: OKEx
providers.description: Cryptocurrency exchange based in Seychelles

providers.name: Alchemix
providers.description: Alchemix is a self-repaying DeFi protocol that allows users to take out interest-free, non-liquidating loans against yield-bearing collateral. Users deposit assets such as ETH, DAI, USDC, or USDT into yield-bearing vaults, and the generated yield automatically repays the loan over time. The protocol issues synthetic alAssets (alUSD, alETH) representing future yield, and provides a Transmuter mechanism to stabilize alAsset prices by gradually exchanging alAssets for underlying collateral. Alchemix operates on Ethereum Mainnet, Optimism, and Arbitrum, with V3 in active development targeting 90% LTV and Meta-Yield Tokens.

providers.name: Andalusia Labs
providers.description: Andalusia Labs is an applied research laboratory headquartered in Palo Alto building internet-native economic infrastructure. Its flagship platform, OpenGDP, is the "Global Base Layer for Programmable GDP" — an EVM-compatible execution layer and network stack for moving value (stablecoin settlement), programming assets (tokenized securities, deposits, and commodities), and orchestrating real-world economic workflows across enterprises, financial institutions, and governments with institutional-grade privacy, compliance, and audit controls. OpenGDP ships developer documentation (build applications, build networks, run validators), a live demo, and a smart-contract bug-bounty program. Backed by Pantera Capital, Founders Fund, Naval Ravikant, Anthony Pompliano, and the co-founders of Alchemy.

providers.name: Goldsky
providers.description: Goldsky is a blockchain data platform that provides managed indexing, streaming, and RPC infrastructure for EVM and non-EVM chains. Core products are Subgraphs (hosted GraphQL indexers compatible with The Graph), Mirror (change-data-capture streaming of onchain data into customer databases and data warehouses), Turbo (vectorized real-time data pipelines with SQL transforms), Compose (orchestration of onchain-x-offchain workflows), and Edge RPC (high-performance EVM RPC with debug and trace). Developers interact via a CLI, a web dashboard, and REST + GraphQL APIs. Sinks supported include PostgreSQL, ClickHouse, Kafka, MySQL, Webhooks, S3, AWS SQS, Elasticsearch, S2, and Parquet.

providers.name: Halborn
providers.description: Halborn is a blockchain and digital-asset cybersecurity firm that sells professional security services rather than a developer product. Its assurance practice covers smart contract assessments, Layer 1 protocol reviews, code security audits, web application and cloud infrastructure penetration testing, red team exercises, and custody and key management assessments; its advisory practice covers AI security, blockchain architecture, compliance readiness, risk assessment, technical due diligence and technical training for banks, exchanges, custodians, tokenization platforms, stablecoin issuers, DeFi protocols, central banks and blockchain infrastructure providers. Halborn publishes its engagement results as a public audit repository, discloses zero-day findings under its own CVE assignment scope as a CVE Numbering Authority, and maintains BVSS, the Blockchain Vulnerability Scoring System. As of August 2026 it publishes no public API, no developer portal and no machine-readable contract; its Halborn ONE client platform at one.halborn.com is an invitation-only customer portal.

providers.name: Amber Group
providers.description: Amber Group is a global digital asset financial services firm founded in 2017 by former traditional-finance traders, providing trading, liquidity provision, wealth and asset management, staking, and treasury solutions for institutions and high-net-worth clients. Its institutional platform, Amber Premium (Nasdaq: AMBR), operates from financial hubs including Singapore, Hong Kong, and Dubai, and publishes the Amber Premium Global API service suite so clients can integrate trading, liquidity, and account services into their own systems. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of DCM Ventures, Pantera Capital, and Paradigm and enriched with the company's public developer, legal, and support surfaces.

providers.name: Anoma
providers.description: Anoma is a distributed operating system that abstracts blockchain complexity into a single intent-centric interface, letting developers build applications once and run them across any chain. It introduces generalized intents for improved UX, programmable and compliance-ready privacy, and the Anoma Resource Machine (ARM) for native intents, interoperability, and scaling. Anoma ships the TypeScript Anoma App SDK (@anomaorg/anoma-app-sdk) with typed HTTP API clients for transfers, on-chain resource indexing, and public-nullifier queries that power Anoma Pay and related privacy applications. Originally added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub, this profile has been enriched from Anoma's public developer surface.

providers.name: Cozy Finance
providers.description: Cozy Finance is a decentralized finance (DeFi) risk-management protocol that helps onchain protocols unlock safety-seeking capital through composable, institutional-grade coverage. Its Cozy Safety Module (CSM) lets teams deploy onchain safety modules, rewards managers, and controllers that backstop capital against security incidents and market risk, using mechanisms such as tranching (junior/senior yield), reserves, and market-based protection contracts. The protocol is used by teams around protocols such as Euler, Lido, and Aave, and is backed by Polychain Capital, Electric Capital, Dragonfly, and Coinbase Ventures. The integration surface is Solidity smart contracts documented at csm-docs.cozy.finance, with TypeScript / ethers.js developer guides; there is no REST or HTTP API.

providers.name: Mainframe
providers.description: Mainframe (Mainframe Group, Inc.) is a software development and marketing services company building products for the decentralized finance (DeFi) ecosystem. It offers three service areas — Risk Management (protocol parameter optimization and stability), Development (DeFi and blockchain financial solutions), and Marketing (brand reach and audience engagement) — and has produced projects including Hifi, Pooled NFT, Sheet Heads, and Crown Ribbon. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and Techstars and added to the API Evangelist network. Mainframe itself publishes only a three-page Webflow marketing site, with no API host and no developer portal (api., docs. and developer.mainframe.co do not resolve), and its MainframeHQ GitHub organization has zero public repositories. Its developer surface lives under its Hifi product instead — the docs.hifi.finance protocol documentation (footer copyright "Mainframe Group Inc."), the github.com/hifi-finance organization, five first-party npm packages in the @hifi scope, and a GraphQL subgraph schema for the Hifi lending protocol. That surface is a smart-contract SDK rather than an HTTP API — there is no REST API and no OpenAPI anywhere — and it has gone quiet, with the newest package release dated 2024-01-12 and the documented GraphQL endpoint on The Graph's retired hosted service returning HTTP 404.

providers.name: Bitfinex
providers.description: Cryptocurrency Trading Platform

providers.name: Fluidity
providers.description: Fluidity Money is a decentralized finance (DeFi) protocol that turns idle crypto into "Fluid Assets" (fAssets) — ERC-20-compatible wrapped tokens on Ethereum/Arbitrum and SPL tokens on Solana that pay instant, probabilistic rewards every time they are transferred (the Transfer Reward Function). Yield is sourced from lending protocols such as Compound and AAVE on Ethereum and Solend on Solana, and distributed through "utility mining." Fluidity exposes a public GraphQL API over its webapp and landing-page data, publishes EVM ABIs and Solana program/account structures for on-chain integration, and is governed by the $FLY token. Fluidity Labs sunsetted active protocol development on 2026-04-01 to focus on the Superposition ecosystem; docs, status page, and on-chain contracts remain live.

providers.name: Gateio
providers.description: API provides spot, margin and futures trading operations

providers.name: Keyrock
providers.description: Keyrock is a digital asset market maker and liquidity provider founded in Brussels in 2017 and now operating as a global crypto investment group. It runs in-house algorithmic and high-frequency trading infrastructure to supply market making, over-the-counter (OTC) trading, an options desk, onchain/DEX liquidity, validator services, ecosystem development and a Smart Beta fund to token issuers, exchanges, brokerages and institutional counterparties across 85+ centralised and decentralised venues. Keyrock also publishes proprietary crypto, FX, commodity and US equity pricing into the Pyth Network oracle. Its commercial surface is bilateral rather than self-serve: engagements are contracted, and clients receive execution analytics and PnL attribution through a credentialed dashboard. As of this profiling round Keyrock publishes no public developer portal, API reference or machine-readable contract of any kind. The group holds a MiCA licence through its French entity Keyrock FR SAS and has publicly announced SOC 2 Type II compliance.

providers.name: PicPay
providers.description: PicPay is a Brazilian fintech super-app and digital bank serving over 67 million users with a digital wallet, payment account, credit and debit cards, personal loans, investments (Cofrinho / fixed income), insurance, and PIX-based money movement. Founded in 2012 and acquired by J&F Investimentos (the holding company behind JBS) in 2015, PicPay is controlled today by J&F Participações and in 2024 incorporated the retail customer base of Banco Original to consolidate the group's consumer banking strategy. For developers and merchants, PicPay Business exposes a set of REST APIs that let online stores accept the PicPay wallet, credit/debit cards, PIX, and payment links as payment methods. The historical Ecommerce Public API on appws.picpay.com is authenticated with the x-picpay-token / x-seller-token headers and remains in use for direct wallet checkout. A newer unified business developer portal at developers-business.picpay.com publishes the Gateway PicPay Checkout API, Carteira PicPay Wallet API, PIX API, and Payment Link API, all of which now use OAuth 2.0 client_credentials bearer JWTs minted at api.picpay.com/oauth2/token (5-minute TTL) and webhook callbacks for payment status notifications. PicPay also publishes GitHub repos for Magento, Shopify, and Wake ecommerce integrations, plus its open developer documentation for the wallet and PIX APIs under picpay.github.io. PicPay reported a return to profitability in 2023 and is reportedly working with Citigroup on a U.S. IPO.

providers.name: INFINIT
providers.description: INFINIT is an AI application for Web3 financial execution that lets anyone research, create, and execute DeFi and trading strategies through AI agents. Its Prompt-to-DeFi experience turns natural-language intents into agent-powered, one-workflow on-chain strategies, and its AI-managed trading vault marketplace lets independent strategy managers deploy non-custodial vaults that depositors access through a single workflow. For developers, INFINIT publishes the open-source INFINIT Library and INFINIT CLI — a TypeScript action framework and command-line tool for programmatically deploying and interacting with DeFi protocols including Aave v3, Uniswap v3, Pendle, and INIT Capital, distributed as npm packages under the @infinit-xyz scope. Backed by Electric Capital and EQT Ventures.

providers.name: marginfi
providers.description: marginfi is a decentralized borrowing and lending protocol built on the Solana blockchain by mrgn labs. Users lend supported Solana tokens to earn yield and borrow against supplied collateral, with account-health, e-mode, liquid staking token (LST), and leveraged looping (mrgnloop) products layered on top of the core mrgnlend market. marginfi exposes no hosted REST API — developers integrate on-chain through the marginfi-v2 Solana program using the official TypeScript SDK (marginfi-client-v2, mrgn-common) and the Rust (CLI) SDK, with an early-alpha Python SDK (marginpy) and a Rust CPI interface crate also published. It was surfaced through the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Multicoin Capital and Pantera Capital.

providers.name: Redotpay
providers.description: RedotPay is a global stablecoin-based payment fintech that integrates blockchain solutions with traditional banking and finance infrastructures. The platform lets millions of people spend and send digital assets through a crypto-backed Visa card, a multi-currency wallet, P2P trading, international transfers, and stablecoin earning. Its developer-facing surface is agentic: a first-party Rust CLI (redotpay) and a local MCP server / Agent Skill (redotpay-payment) that let AI agents settle HTTP 402 "Payment Required" challenges over the Machine Payments Protocol (MPP), using OAuth2 device-flow login and per-payment idempotency against the production RedotPay API.

providers.name: Royco
providers.description: Royco is a decentralized finance (DeFi) protocol offering transparent, structured yield markets for capital allocators. Through Royco Dawn, users allocate capital into tranched yield markets - senior tranches prioritize base yield with first-loss protection, junior tranches accept first loss for amplified yield - or delegate allocation to independent curators via vaults, with Loop leverage and a coming secondary market and fixed-rate structures. All deposits flow through the RoycoEntryPoint gateway, deployed on Ethereum and Avalanche, with critical upgrades gated by 3-of-5 council approval and timelocks. The protocol has undergone 5 independent audits and formal verifications (Hexens, Cantina, Certora, Nethermind, Immunefi) and ships an official TypeScript SDK plus subgraphs for building frontends on top of it.

providers.name: Quant Network
providers.description: Quant Network is a blockchain interoperability company whose Overledger platform provides APIs to issue, connect, and monitor digital assets, smart contracts, transactions, and accounts across multiple distributed ledger technologies without requiring blockchain expertise.

providers.name: Cartesi
providers.description: Cartesi is a Linux-based optimistic rollup protocol that lets developers build decentralized applications by running rich off-chain computation inside a sandboxed Linux virtual machine. The core of the stack is the Cartesi Machine, a deterministic RISC-V emulator that boots a real Linux userland so dApps can be written in any language (Rust, Go, Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, C++) using familiar libraries, then settle results on Ethereum and other EVM chains through Cartesi Rollups smart contracts. Cartesi Rollups 2.0 is the current major version, packaging an application-specific rollup as the combination of the Cartesi Machine, the Cartesi Rollups Node middleware (Rust + Go), and a set of Solidity rollup contracts that handle settlement, consensus, and data availability. The DAVE permissionless fraud-proof system provides Stage-2 trust minimization, while the Cartesi CLI (the successor to Sunodo) packages scaffolding, build, and local devnet workflows. Cartesi is stewarded by The Cartesi Foundation and the CTSI token governs the network. Cartesi is fully open source under Apache-2.0 and LGPL-3.0 licenses on github.com/cartesi; there is no proprietary SaaS product, but the Rollups Node ships several developer-facing surfaces — the Rollup HTTP API used by application backends, the Inspect HTTP API for read-only queries from frontends, a GraphQL reader for advance-state inputs / outputs / vouchers / notices / reports, and a JSON-RPC node API for operations.

providers.name: Coinigy
providers.description: Interacting with Coinigy Accounts and Exchange Directly

providers.name: Multipli
providers.description: Multipli is a decentralized yield-infrastructure protocol that lets users and institutions generate returns on tokenized real-world assets — gold, stocks, commodities and stablecoins — without selling their holdings. Its native rwaUSD token consolidates 100+ Treasury-backed stablecoins and 10+ tokenized gold assets into a single, standardized collateral primitive that can move freely across DeFi, earning yield through delta-neutral arbitrage (contango and funding-rate) strategies. Integration is smart-contract-based across multiple EVM chains via a suite of on-chain view functions (Ledger, RiskRegistry, PriceRouter); there is no public REST API, SDK or OpenAPI. Multipli is backed by Pantera Capital.

providers.name: Bybit
providers.description: Cryptocurrency data feed and algorithmic trading

providers.name: Coinbase OnchainKit
providers.description: Coinbase OnchainKit is a TypeScript React framework from Coinbase for building onchain applications on Base and other EVM networks. It bundles ready-made React components (wallets, identity, transactions, swap, checkout, fund, NFT), TypeScript utilities, and integrations with Smart Wallet, Base Account, Frames, and Mini Apps. OnchainKit is distributed as the @coinbase/onchainkit npm package along with companion CLIs (create-onchain) and a MiniApp manifest generator. It is built on top of Wagmi, Viem, and TailwindCSS and is the recommended client SDK for the Base ecosystem.

providers.name: EZKL
providers.description: EZKL (by Zkonduit Inc.) is a developer-friendly engine for verifiable AI and analytics that generates zero-knowledge proofs (ZK-SNARKs, Halo2) for machine learning model inference. Given a model in ONNX format and sample input, EZKL automatically compiles a proving circuit and produces a cryptographic proof that a computation ran correctly without revealing the underlying private data or model weights. Proofs are verifiable on-chain (EVM-compatible), in the browser, or on edge devices. EZKL ships as a command-line tool, Python and JavaScript (WebAssembly) bindings, and a Rust library, and supports tree-based models, transformers, CNNs, and RNNs. Lilith is its high-performance compute cluster for cloud-scale proof generation. The codebase was audited by Trail of Bits and is developed in the open at github.com/zkonduit/ezkl.

providers.name: Poloniex
providers.description: US based digital asset exchange

providers.name: BlockVision
providers.description: BlockVision is a Web3 data infrastructure provider offering multi-chain node, indexing, and on-chain data-retrieval APIs for developers building decentralized applications. Its stack includes an Indexing API service (real-time account, coin/token, NFT, DeFi, DEX-market and smart-contract data across Sui, Monad, Ethereum, Arbitrum, BNB Chain, Optimism and Polygon), an RPC Node service (AceNode) with geo-distributed low-latency and archive access, a gRPC endpoint for Sui, and Explorer-as-a-Service (branded block explorers such as SuiVision and BBScan). Requests to the Data API (api.blockvision.org, versioned under /v2) are authenticated with an x-api-key header and metered in Compute Units. Originally added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Qiming, this profile has been enriched from BlockVision's public developer surface.

providers.name: Unisub LLC
providers.description: UniSub is a recurring crypto-payments platform that lets merchants accept automated on-chain subscriptions and deposits directly from customer wallets (MetaMask, WalletConnect, Coinbase Wallet) in USDT, USDC, DAI, WBTC, WETH and other ERC20/Polygon tokens across EVM-compatible chains. Subscriptions are executed by audited smart contracts, and merchants integrate through an embeddable payment widget, checkout links, or per-merchant API/webhooks, with a hosted dashboard for subscribers and analytics. A 500 Global portfolio company based in Batumi, Georgia, UniSub also publishes its SubscriptionApp smart contracts and a The Graph subgraph on GitHub.

providers.name: Arch Network
providers.description: Arch Network is Bitcoin-native financial infrastructure and a computation environment that lets developers build DeFi and capital-markets applications — lending, yield, trading, and structured products — with settlement kept local to Bitcoin. It executes programmable smart contracts (written in Rust) over Bitcoin UTXOs using a specialized virtual machine and threshold-cryptography (FROST/ROAST) validator security, and exposes a JSON-RPC API with first-party TypeScript and Rust SDKs, a CLI, and an AI agent kit. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Multicoin Capital.

providers.name: Convex Finance
providers.description: Convex Finance is a DeFi protocol that boosts Curve Finance liquidity provider and CRV staker yields through its CVX token and pooled staking mechanism. It allows users to earn boosted CRV rewards and CVX without locking CRV directly.

providers.name: Sunscreen
providers.description: Sunscreen is a cryptography company building the Secure Processing Framework (SPF) — an end-to-end platform for Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) on blockchain. SPF lets web2 and web3 developers write programs, compile them to the Parasol FHE processor, and run them over encrypted data on-chain without ever exposing plaintext. The stack includes the open-source Sunscreen FHE/ZKP compiler (a family of Rust crates on crates.io), the Parasol processor runtime, a TypeScript SDK (@sunscreen/spf-client) and a Rust CLI for encrypting values, uploading FHE programs and ciphertexts, requesting threshold decryption, and managing on-chain access control (ACL). Founded by cryptographers and engineers from Nucypher, Microsoft, Meta, Tableau, Two Sigma and Caldera, and backed by Northzone.

providers.name: Wynd Network
providers.description: Wynd Network (now operating as Wynd Labs) is the company behind Grass, a decentralized physical infrastructure network (DePIN) on Solana that rewards users for sharing their unused internet bandwidth. The Grass Network routes and verifies web traffic through a network of nodes, routers, and validators to collect and structure public web data for AI training and business intelligence. Grass ships consumer apps and a node network rather than a public developer API; its documentation covers network architecture, the GRASS token, staking, and points.

providers.name: DODO
providers.description: DODO is a decentralized exchange (DEX) and on-chain liquidity provider built on the Proactive Market Maker (PMM) algorithm, engineered for capital-efficient liquidity and low slippage across many EVM blockchains. Its Trade / Route API aggregates prices across DODO v1/v2, 1inch, 0x, ParaSwap, professional market makers, and DODO's own aggregation algorithm, returning real-time swap quotes plus executable ABI calldata that developers send directly to the DODORouteProxy / DODOV2Proxy contracts. DODO is backed by Pantera Capital and ships open-source smart contracts, JavaScript/TypeScript SDKs, a contract request library, and embeddable swap widgets.

providers.name: InfinitySwap
providers.description: InfinitySwap is now Bitfinity Network, a next-generation Ethereum Virtual Machine (EVM) that serves as a Layer 2 for Bitcoin and Bitcoin on-chain assets, built on the Internet Computer (ICP). Bitfinity delivers high-throughput (1000+ TPS) EVM execution with full Ethereum tooling compatibility (MetaMask, Remix, Hardhat) exposed through a standard Ethereum JSON-RPC endpoint, letting developers deploy Solidity smart contracts and bridge BTC, ckBTC, and other assets. The project also maintains the Bitfinity Wallet, the Bitfusion bridging SDK, canister SDKs for the Internet Computer, and the InfinitySwap decentralized exchange heritage. Backed by Polychain, it targets DeFi builders who want Bitcoin-secured, EVM-compatible infrastructure.

providers.name: KuCoin
providers.description: Cryptocurrency Trading Platform

providers.name: Dabba
providers.description: Dabba (Wifi Dabba) is a Web3-powered decentralized physical infrastructure network (DePIN) that brings affordable internet connectivity to emerging markets, starting in India. It deploys low-cost Dabba Lite WiFi hotspots through a network of local cable operators (LCOs) and rewards hotspot owners, location owners, backhaul providers, and hardware manufacturers with DBT tokens as data is consumed. Network activity — NFTs, subscriber revenue, and bandwidth usage — is reported onchain, and the token flows through a mint, buyback, and burn model. Surfaced as a Multicoin Capital portfolio company; profiled here from public developer, documentation, and onchain surfaces.

providers.name: FastLane
providers.description: FastLane Labs is a blockchain infrastructure provider building maximal extractable value (MEV) and liquid staking products on the Monad blockchain. Its core products are shMON, a liquid staking token that pairs staking rewards with revenue from FastLane's on-chain MEV auction and holds the majority of Monad's liquid-staking TVL; Smart Vault, a USDC-denominated yield product; and hMON, a yield-donation token. FastLane operates a public, on-chain MEV auction that a majority of Monad validators route blocks through, exposing developer surfaces for searchers (the FastLane Sidecar and auction-handler contracts), validators (a Leader API and validator onboarding), and stakers. It also maintains Atlas, an open-source execution-abstraction framework, with a Go SDK and JSON-RPC tooling published on GitHub. Developer integration is via JSON-RPC APIs and Solidity smart contracts rather than a REST/OpenAPI catalog.

providers.name: Offchain
providers.description: Offchain (formerly Offchain Labs) is a blockchain infrastructure company that builds and maintains core technology for the Ethereum ecosystem. It is the creator of Arbitrum, the leading Ethereum layer-2 scaling solution offering high throughput with Ethereum-grade security; Prysm, a Go implementation of the Ethereum proof-of-stake consensus client that powers roughly a quarter of the network's consensus nodes; and Stylus, which lets developers write smart contracts in Rust, C, and C++ compiled to WebAssembly. Offchain also operates ZeroDev (smart-account / ERC-4337 account-abstraction infrastructure) and the Arbitrum (Orbit) chain SDK for launching custom layer-2 and layer-3 chains. The developer surface is Ethereum-compatible JSON-RPC plus first-party TypeScript and Solidity libraries published under the @arbitrum npm scope; the company does not expose a single hosted REST API. Backed by Redpoint Ventures.

providers.name: Puffer Finance
providers.description: Puffer Finance is an Ethereum infrastructure protocol building native liquid restaking (nLRP) integrated with EigenLayer, the UniFi based rollup, and Puffer Preconf preconfirmation services. Users stake ETH to mint the pufETH liquid restaking token and earn Ethereum staking plus EigenLayer and Puffer restaking yields. Puffer also ships institutional-grade staking infrastructure. It is an onchain, smart-contract protocol: developers integrate via its Solidity contracts, the first-party TypeScript puffer-sdk, and the Rust coral CLI rather than a hosted web API. Surfaced as a portfolio company of electric-capital and enriched in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Chaoslabs
providers.description: Chaos Labs is a New York-based company building financial-intelligence and economic-security infrastructure for onchain markets. Its flagship product, Edge (Chaos Oracles), is a decentralized oracle protocol that unifies real-time price, risk, and proof-of-reserves data, delivering high-precision price feeds with an integrated risk engine plus automated, real-time risk-parameter optimization. Leading DeFi protocols including Aave, GMX, dYdX, Jupiter, Venus, Lido, Maker and Uniswap Foundation use Chaos Labs to help secure billions of dollars in value. Developer integration spans EVM, SVM, off-chain services and TradingView via docs.chaoslabs.xyz. Founded in 2021 by Omer Goldberg and Julian Lindinger, Chaos Labs is backed by Haun Ventures, Galaxy, PayPal Ventures, Coinbase Ventures, Lightspeed, Bessemer and others, and holds ISO/IEC 27001 certification. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners and enriched from Chaos Labs' real public developer surface.

providers.name: Mountain Protocol
providers.description: Mountain Protocol is the issuer of USDM, a regulated, institutional-grade yield-bearing stablecoin backed by short-term US Treasury securities that pays daily rewards to holders through an ERC20 rebasing token. The company operated a Primary-User account platform with a private REST API for depositing and withdrawing USDM and USDC, querying account balances, and checking USDC liquidity, alongside on-chain proof-of-reserves and a smart-contract security program audited by OpenZeppelin with an Immunefi bug bounty. As of 2025 the protocol entered an orderly wind-down: the primary market closed on August 22, 2025, redemptions moved to secondary markets, and Phase 3 provides on-chain proof-of-reserves so holders can independently verify USDM backing. Backed by Multicoin Capital.

providers.name: String Technology Inc
providers.description: String (string.xyz) is a fiat interoperability platform for Web3 gaming, operated by String Technology Inc and backed by 500 Global. String lets game developers accept credit-card and bank payments natively inside their games, acting as the merchant of record and counterparty for fiat on/off ramps, NFT purchases, and cross-chain payments. A player pays fiat on traditional rails and String delivers the digital asset on-chain — either by interacting with the game's smart contract to mint/send an NFT or by sending a token from its treasury to the player's wallet. String ships three integration surfaces — String Checkout (drop-in payment app), a Unity SDK, and String Direct (custom web SDK) — all wrapping a REST API at string-api.xyz that covers API keys, contracts, platforms (games), members, organizations, users (players), saved cards, wallet-signature login, quotes, and transactions.

providers.name: Ready (formerly Argent)
providers.description: Ready (formerly Argent) is a self-custodial crypto wallet and smart-account platform for Starknet and Ethereum. It builds account-abstraction wallets (Ready Wallet, Ready Multisig, Web Wallet), the Ready Card for cashing out, and developer tooling for dApps — session keys, paymasters / gas abstraction, outside execution, multicalls, and signature/cosigner verification — shipped as first-party client SDKs (StarknetKit, @argent/x-sessions, web3.swift, starknet.swift). The company rebranded from Argent to Ready; developer resources live at docs.ready.co and the argentlabs GitHub organization. Its developer surface is client SDKs rather than a public REST API.

providers.name: The Giving Block
providers.description: The Giving Block is a crypto-native fundraising platform that lets nonprofits and enterprises accept cryptocurrency, stock, and card donations. Through its Public API and embeddable donation widget, partners can build their own donation experiences or embed The Giving Block's donation form to route gifts to more than 1,000 nonprofit organizations in its network. The API securely accepts Bitcoin, Ethereum, and 100+ other cryptocurrencies, instantly converts crypto donations to cash so nonprofits never have to touch crypto, and also supports stock and donor-advised-fund (DAF) giving. It is a RESTful, JSON API with JWT-based authentication, AES-256 encrypted webhook notifications, and separate production and sandbox environments. The Giving Block was surfaced as a portfolio company of Multicoin Capital and enriched into the API Evangelist network from its published developer documentation.

providers.name: Infinifi
providers.description: infiniFi (InfiniFi Labs) is a DeFi protocol that amplifies returns on existing DeFi yield platforms — Pendle, Ethena, AAVE, and others it calls "farms" — by applying fractional-reserve banking principles on-chain. Users deposit USDC to mint iUSD (a receipt token), then stake it for siUSD (liquid yield) or lock it for liUSD (illiquid yield plus governance). liUSD holders govern capital allocation across liquid, maturity, and protocol farms through allocation voting weighted by locked amount and unwinding period. The protocol is a set of timelock-governed, audited Solidity smart contracts (Core, Gateway, Funding, Locking, YieldSharing, FarmRegistry) on Ethereum, backed by Electric Capital.

providers.name: Faraway
providers.description: Faraway is a web3 gaming company building an interoperable gaming ecosystem for players, creators, and studios. Its platform lets game studios integrate player-driven, blockchain-based economies into their titles across EVM-compatible chains and Solana, with a unified player identity and wallet (id.faraway.com), a creator platform for user-generated content and monetization (create.faraway.com), and an in-game marketplace and secondary-trading shop (shop.faraway.com). Faraway publishes a developer platform with an API reference and an llms.txt index at docs.faraway.com. The company is backed by a16z, Lightspeed Venture Partners, and Pantera Capital.

providers.name: Karak
providers.description: Karak — now operating as OpenGDP — is a blockchain infrastructure project incubated by Andalusia Labs and backed by Pantera Capital. Originally a universal restaking protocol (K2 / v1 + v2 staking), it has rebranded to OpenGDP, positioned as a global base layer for programmable GDP: an EVM-compatible execution layer unifying stablecoin settlement, real-world asset tokenization, and autonomous economic workflow orchestration for enterprises, institutions, and governments. The stack spans the OpenGDP Network (base execution layer with adaptive multi-proposers, automatic fee swaps, dedicated blockspace, native orderbook, private transactions, and stablecoin gas), the OpenGDP Network Stack (ONS) for launching bespoke economic networks, and a platform layer for moving value, programming assets, and orchestrating GDP. It exposes on-chain/EVM infrastructure (precompiles, validators, the K2 bridge) rather than a hosted REST API; developer resources are published at docs.opengdp.network.

providers.name: Co:Create
providers.description: Co:Create (operated by Gesso Labs, Inc.) was an a16z crypto-backed web3 platform that gave brands and developers a REST API to build and run token-driven loyalty, rewards, and community programs on the Polygon blockchain. Its API-first toolkit let teams create and manage users and hosted wallets, deploy and manage ERC-20, ERC-721, ERC-1155, and Soulbound token contracts, mint and transfer tokens (with synchronous and asynchronous variants plus status polling), run reward Campaigns with built-in business logic, issue Referrals, and offer Redemptions, Auctions, and Prize Draws. It also provided NFT media/metadata hosting, fiat and crypto checkout (via a Crossmint integration), a Co:Create SDK, and Shopify/Salesforce integrations. The public developer surface (docs.usecocreate.io, api.cocrt.xyz) is now offline; this profile is reconstructed from the provider's own published documentation (archived) and preserved for the network.

providers.name: MoreMarkets
providers.description: MoreMarkets is a self-custodial, cross-chain DeFi yield platform that lets holders of assets like XRP and DOGE earn institutional-grade yield without giving up custody of their funds. It uses Multi-Party Computation (MPC) key management and NEAR chain signatures to lock native assets in onchain vaults (a BoringVault-based architecture with tellers, managers, and principal/receipt/positional tokens) and deploy equivalent tokens across chains into DeFi lending and yield strategies, bridged via Wormhole and the Omni Bridge. In July 2025 it launched the XRP Earn Account and later partnered with Flare for additional XRP yield strategies. Backed by Electric Capital.

providers.name: Unlonely
providers.description: Unlonely was a crypto/web3 livestreaming platform founded by Grace and Brian Guan and backed by Multicoin Capital — livestreams on Base with token-gated chat, creator and temp tokens, the $VIBES on-chain interaction economy, and stream clips minted as NFCs (non-fungible clips). The product is defunct: the unlonely.app domain registration has expired and the hosted GraphQL API is no longer live, but the platform was open source and this profile preserves its real GraphQL schema (225 types) harvested from the public monorepo.

providers.name: Ellipsis Labs
providers.description: Ellipsis Labs builds decentralized finance applications and infrastructure on Solana. Its flagship product is Phoenix, a fully on-chain, atomically-settled limit order book exchange for spot assets, now expanded with Phoenix Perps for on-chain perpetual futures. The team also develops Atlas (a high-performance DeFi Layer 2), Gavel (token distribution and liquidity bootstrapping), and Plasma (a sandwich-resistant AMM reference implementation). Ellipsis exposes its protocol to developers through open-source SDKs (TypeScript, Rust, Python), command-line tools, and on-chain Solana programs rather than a hosted REST API. Backed by Electric Capital and Paradigm.

providers.name: Obligate
providers.description: Obligate (formerly FQX) is a Swiss digital-securities infrastructure provider for regulated on-chain debt capital markets. Its AssetOS platform lets companies issue tokenized bonds and short-term notes as blockchain-based eNotes and eTrackers under the Swiss DLT Act and Code of Obligations, while institutional investors access regulated on-chain private credit, asset-backed securities and trade-finance yield products. Obligate automates the bond lifecycle with smart contracts across multiple blockchains, with built-in KYB/KYC, settlement and enforcement, reducing issuance cost and time versus traditional debt issuance.

providers.name: Compound Finance
providers.description: Compound is a decentralized, blockchain-based protocol that allows users to lend and borrow cryptocurrencies (DeFi lending protocol) built on Ethereum.

providers.name: Beefy Finance
providers.description: Beefy Finance is a decentralized, multichain yield optimizer platform that allows users to earn compound interest on their crypto holdings through automated vaults and strategies.

providers.name: Jeeves
providers.description: Jeeves is a global financial platform for cross-border businesses, combining corporate cards (physical and virtual with spend controls and cashback), automated expense management with approval flows and policy enforcement, cross-border payments and transfers to 150+ countries in 40+ currencies, instant and stablecoin-based settlement, non-dilutive corporate credit, and AI-driven spend insights. Jeeves operates across Brazil, Colombia, Mexico, Canada, the USA, the UK, and the European Union, serving globally operating companies. Backed by a16z and CRV, the company is tracked in the API Evangelist network; no public developer API or documentation surface was found at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: Lightning Labs
providers.description: At Lightning Labs, we develop software that powers the Lightning Network. Our open source, secure, and scalable Lightning systems enable users to send and receive money more efficiently than ever before. We also offer a series of verifiable, non-custodial Lightning-based financial services. We bridge the world of open source software and the next-generation of bitcoin financial software.

providers.name: Pipe Network
providers.description: Pipe Network is a decentralized storage and content-delivery network built on Solana, marketed as "Firestarter" storage. It offers content-addressed (Blake3) object storage with client-side AES-256-GCM and post-quantum (Kyber-1024 / Dilithium5) encryption, deterministic public URLs of the form /{account}/{hash}, prepaid-USDC billing funded via Solana Pay, and first-party TypeScript / Python / Rust SDKs plus a Rust CLI. The SDKs ship native agent- framework tool adapters (OpenAI, Anthropic, LangChain, LlamaIndex, Vercel AI SDK, Cloudflare AI Workflows, AutoGen, CrewAI) and x402 machine-to-machine payment support. Backed by Multicoin Capital.

providers.name: Balancer
providers.description: Balancer is a DeFi AMM and programmable liquidity platform supporting weighted, stable, and custom pools (v2 and v3). Balancer publishes a public GraphQL API at api-v3.balancer.fi for pool, swap, and analytics data, plus per-chain subgraph endpoints. Smart-contract entry points (Vault and Router) are the primary write surface; SDKs wrap the SOR (Smart Order Router) for client-side route construction.

providers.name: DolarApp
providers.description: DolarApp — rebranded to ARQ in March 2026 — is a Latin American cross-border fintech founded in Mexico in 2022 by former Revolut operators Fernando Terres, Zach Garman and Alvaro Correa. It gives consumers and businesses in Mexico, Argentina, Colombia and Brazil digital dollar (USDc) and euro (EURc) accounts, US ACH/wire receiving details, international cards accepted in 180+ countries, interbank-rate FX conversion, bulk supplier and contractor payouts, corporate cards with spend controls, and investment and credit products. It reports roughly two million users and is backed by Sequoia Capital, Founders Fund, Brevan Howard Digital, Y Combinator and Kaszek. DolarApp/ARQ runs a private API host at api.dolarapp.com for its own mobile and web applications but publishes no public developer program, documentation or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Integral
providers.description: Integral (Integral Development Corp.) is a technology provider for institutional currency and digital-asset trading. Its cloud-native, API-first platform delivers liquidity aggregation, execution management, pricing engines, distribution, risk management, settlement, and market data across foreign exchange, CFDs, precious metals, and crypto. Integral serves banks, institutional and retail brokers, precious-metals businesses, and crypto trading firms, and is SOC 2 Type II certified with connectivity over FIX, ITCH, and proprietary REST and WebSocket APIs. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel, Electric Capital, and General Catalyst.

providers.name: big xyt
providers.description: big xyt AG (now branded simply xyt, with big-xyt.com redirecting to xyt.one) is an independent, majority employee-owned market data analytics firm headquartered in Frankfurt am Main, Germany.
