It sells tick-data-driven market intelligence covering equities, ETFs, listed derivatives, FX, and fixed income across 120+ venues, processing 12bn+ messages per day with roughly ten years of history at nanosecond precision and market-by-order granularity. Products include the Liquidity Cockpit (market share and liquidity analytics), Transaction Cost Analysis against its SMART benchmark, pre-trade cost modeling, a Datashop of analysis-ready datasets and APIs, and an xyt AI natural-language query layer. Three API products are publicly named - the big xyt API, Liquidity Cockpit API, and TCA API - but their reference documentation sits behind a login at docs.big-xyt.com (HTTP 403 unauthenticated), and access is sales-gated via a book-a-demo motion with no self-serve signup, public pricing, or public OpenAPI.

providers.name: Flowdesk
providers.description: Flowdesk is a full-service digital-asset trading and technology firm that delivers liquidity, execution, and market infrastructure to token issuers, exchanges, and institutions. It is a regulated Crypto-Asset Service Provider registered with France's AMF and licensed by Dubai's Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority (VARA). Products span liquidity solutions (token, stablecoin, exchange, and DeFi), OTC trading (spot, derivatives, and credit) across 150+ venues and 1,000+ asset pairs, tokenized-market infrastructure, and ventures. Flowdesk exposes a developer-facing "Platform Connect" API for programmatic OTC spot trading over REST with a companion WebSocket streaming channel, authenticated with OAuth 2.0 JWT bearer tokens issued through its Auth0 tenant.

providers.name: Rain (Raincards)
providers.description: Rain is a stablecoin payments infrastructure company that lets platforms, fintechs, and institutions issue cards, open virtual accounts and wallets, and move money globally through a single API. Its issuing platform turns self-custodied stablecoin collateral and digital-dollar balances into Visa/Mastercard-accepted spending at over 175 million merchant locations, connecting blockchain settlement rails to traditional card networks. Products include card issuing, corporate/spend cards, virtual accounts, onramps and offramps, and cross-border payment processing. Rain is a Mastercard Principal Member and is backed by Norwest Venture Partners, Sapphire Ventures, Lightspeed, and Coinbase Ventures. The public developer surface is a gated Mintlify documentation portal at docs.rain.xyz covering the Rain Issuing API; the OpenAPI/Swagger reference is behind login and not publicly retrievable.

providers.name: Entropy
providers.description: Entropy is a threshold-signature network for trustless, programmable key management and distributed key generation (DKG). Positioned as "the Autonomous Agent Network," Entropy lets users and agents produce cryptographic signatures without any single party ever holding the private key, using on-chain WASM "programs" that define the exact conditions under which a signature may be generated. Built as a Substrate-based blockchain with a network of Threshold Signature Scheme (TSS) servers running inside Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs), Entropy delivers secure crypto custody, programmable signing, and distributed key management for Web3 and autonomous-agent use cases. Backed by a16z and surfaced into the API Evangelist network via the venture-portfolio pipeline.

providers.name: Forte Labs
providers.description: Forte builds on-chain compliance and economic tooling for games and Web3 applications. Its flagship developer product, the Forte Rules Engine, is an open-source EVM protocol that lets developers define powerful, flexible, and composable on-chain policies — for regulatory compliance, risk management, and token-economy design — without hardcoding rules into their smart contracts. The engine centers on policies, rules, trackers, and calling/foreign contracts, ships client contracts for the ERC20/721/1155/721A token standards, and is consumed through a TypeScript SDK. Forte was founded in 2019 and is backed by Andreessen Horowitz, Battery Ventures, Griffin Gaming Partners, and Canaan. This profile catalogs Forte's public developer surface — Rules Engine documentation, SDK, and GitHub organization.

providers.name: Ancient8
providers.description: Ancient8 is a gaming-focused Ethereum Layer 2 blockchain built on the Optimism OP Stack with Celestia for data availability, designed to power Web3 gaming experiences at scale. The network is EVM-equivalent, so developers deploy Solidity smart contracts and dApps using standard tooling (Hardhat, Remix, thirdweb) against a public Ethereum JSON-RPC interface. Ancient8 Mainnet uses chain ID 888888888 with ETH as its gas currency, complemented by a Celestia-backed testnet, native and third-party bridges (Meson, Relay), block explorers (Routescan, Blockscout/A8Scan), a faucet, staking, and a vault. The programmable surface exposed to integrators is the JSON-RPC endpoint over HTTPS and WebSocket. Backed by Pantera Capital and surfaced into the API Evangelist network from its venture portfolio.

providers.name: Lithium Finance
providers.description: Lithium Finance is a decentralized asset-pricing protocol that combines machine learning with collective intelligence to value illiquid assets, with an initial focus on NFTs. Quantitative models analyze historical trading data to produce a base valuation and to flag cases where machine learning struggles — such as rare NFTs with little trading history — and the protocol then incentivizes a community of Price Experts to submit pricing estimates through on-chain Pricing Quests. Two ecosystem roles drive the network: Price Seekers (data consumers such as projects, lenders, issuers and analysts) fund prize pools to post asset-pricing enquiries, and Price Experts (brokers, traders and market participants) answer them for bounties. The economy runs on the LITH token plus non-transferable Reputation Points, and the protocol is governed by the Lithium DAO via Snapshot. The public surface is a set of Solidity Enquiry Pool, Reputation and LITH token contracts rather than a hosted web API.

providers.name: Talus Network
providers.description: Talus Network is a decentralized Layer 1 platform for building and running autonomous, verifiable AI agents fully on-chain. Its core product, Nexus, is an agentic workflow engine that lets developers compose agents as directed acyclic graphs (DAGs) of reusable Tools — LLM calls, HTTP requests, storage, exchanges — executed and settled on-chain. Talus is built on Sui Move smart contracts with a Cosmos SDK / CometBFT Protochain node, and ships a developer surface as Rust crates (nexus-sdk, nexus-cli, nexus-toolkit), a Homebrew/AUR CLI, GitBook developer docs, and on-chain Move module API references. Backed by Polychain, Talus positions itself as infrastructure for the autonomous digital economy. There is no traditional REST / OpenAPI HTTP API; the platform is consumed through the SDK, CLI, and Move contracts.

providers.name: Term Finance
providers.description: Term Finance is a noncustodial, fixed-rate lending and borrowing protocol for crypto assets, modeled on the tri-party repo arrangements common in traditional finance (TradFi). Liquidity suppliers and takers are matched through a weekly blind double-auction that aggregates bids and offers into a single market-clearing rate, while collateral backing each loan sits in isolated, non-rehypothecatable smart contracts known as repoLockers. The protocol is deployed across Ethereum, Avalanche, Base, BNB Smart Chain and Plasma, and its Solidity contracts have been audited by Sigma Prime, Runtime Verification, Dedaub and Certora. Term Finance is developer-facing primarily through on-chain smart contracts and a Solidity API reference rather than a hosted REST API.

providers.name: Zama
providers.description: Zama is an open-source cryptography company building state-of-the-art Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) solutions for blockchain and AI. Its developer surface is a suite of libraries and protocols rather than a hosted REST API: TFHE-rs (a Rust implementation of TFHE), Concrete (a Python-to-FHE compiler), Concrete ML (privacy-preserving machine learning), fhEVM and the Zama Protocol for building confidential smart contracts and dApps on EVM-compatible chains, plus TypeScript SDKs (the fhEVM Relayer SDK and React SDK). Zama publishes the ERC-7984 confidential token standard, a developer hub, GitBook documentation, and an active open-source GitHub organization. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Multicoin Capital and enriched from Zama's public developer surface.

providers.name: Catena
providers.description: Catena (Catena Labs) is building a regulated banking and governance platform for AI agents. The platform gives agents verified identities, custodial and non-custodial accounts, fiat and stablecoin payment rails across ten chains, yield on idle assets, and policy-enforced spending controls. For the humans and businesses deploying those agents it is a control plane: set policy, cap spending, restrict counterparties, audit every movement, and halt activity when needed. Agents access the platform through an API, a CLI, an MCP server, and a Skills framework. Founded by Sean Neville (CEO) and Matt Venables (CTO) - both Circle co-founders and creators of USDC - Catena has filed for a National Trust Bank charter with the OCC and raised $48M total ($30M Series A co-led by a16z crypto and Acrew, with QED, Coinbase Ventures, General Catalyst, Breyer Capital, IDG Capital, Oak HC/FT, and Pillar).

providers.name: Chainlink
providers.description: Build hybrid smart contracts with Chainlink

providers.name: Frax Finance
providers.description: Frax Finance is a fractional-algorithmic stablecoin protocol featuring FRAX (a stablecoin), FXS (Frax Shares governance token), and Fraxswap — a TWAMM-based AMM DEX. The protocol is deployed across multiple chains and exposes its on-chain data via The Graph subgraphs.

providers.name: Topl
providers.description: Topl was an impact-technology company founded in 2017 out of Rice University and based in Houston, Texas, building a proof-of-stake blockchain that let organizations prove ethical and sustainable practices on-ledger. It raised a $3M seed in 2020 and a $15M Series A in 2022, and shipped a real developer platform: the Bifrost node, the Genus indexer, the Brambl SDK family for Scala, TypeScript, JavaScript and Dart, and the brambl-cli client. In late 2023 the company rebranded to Apparatus and repositioned around Thunder, a Bitcoin Layer 2. It appears to have wound down after that — the last first-party artifact of any kind shipped on 2024-09-26, all ten remaining public repositories are archived, every documentation and API host now fails to resolve, and the topl.co domain lapsed and was re-registered by an unrelated owner on 2024-12-30. What survives, and what this profile is built from, is the contract itself: a 38-file proto3 module defining 6 gRPC services, 30 RPCs and 138 messages, still downloadable from the Buf Schema Registry, plus the published SDKs and container images.

providers.name: Boku
providers.description: Boku is a global mobile payments network that connects digital merchants to more than 200 local payment methods — mobile wallets, real-time account-to-account bank transfers, and direct carrier billing — across 70+ countries, reaching over 7 billion payment accounts. Through its Boku Direct payment gateway API, merchants such as Epic Games, Google, Meta, Microsoft, Netflix, Sony, Spotify, and Tencent accept local payments, run subscriptions, and settle globally. Boku processes over $9 billion in payments annually and is publicly traded on the London Stock Exchange (LON:BOKU).

providers.name: Courtyard
providers.description: Courtyard (courtyard.io) is a marketplace and tokenization service for physical collectibles — trading cards, luxury watches, and other graded assets. Collectors vault a physical item in Courtyard's insured facility and receive a blockchain-backed digital token (an NFT on Ethereum/Polygon) representing verified ownership, which can then be instantly bought, sold, bid on, or redeemed for physical shipment. The platform combines a "Proof of Integrity" authentication process, KYC-gated onboarding, a hosted wallet with fiat funding, digital pack drops and auctions, and a curated showroom experience. Courtyard is a Forerunner Ventures portfolio company operating in the commerce / collectibles sector; it exposes a consumer web application and smart contracts rather than a public developer API.

providers.name: Magic
providers.description: Magic is an embedded-wallet and authentication platform offering passwordless login (magic links, OAuth, WebAuthn, SMS) plus white-label Embedded Wallets and Server Wallets. Primary surface is the Magic SDK; an Admin REST API exists for user lookup, token validation, and metadata.

providers.name: Media Chain
providers.description: Mediachain (Mediachain Labs) was a decentralized universal media library and attribution protocol built on IPFS and blockchain technology, designed to let creators and applications collaborate on open metadata about creative works and track the provenance and ownership of online images and other media. Founded in 2016 with seed funding from Andreessen Horowitz and Union Square Ventures, the company was acqui-hired by Spotify in April 2017 to help build fair, blockchain-based royalty attribution for rightsholders. The company is now defunct and its primary domain (mediachain.io) is a parked page, but its open-source protocol, design documentation, Protocol Buffer definitions, and first-party client libraries (the `aleph`/`mcclient` JavaScript client on npm and the `mediachain-client` Python reader on PyPI) remain public under the github.com/mediachain organization. This profile was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and enriched from its surviving open-source surface.

providers.name: BitTorrent
providers.description: BitTorrent is the company behind the BitTorrent peer-to-peer file-sharing protocol and the uTorrent and BitTorrent desktop and web torrent clients, one of the most widely deployed distributed content-delivery technologies on the internet. Now part of the TRON ecosystem, BitTorrent also operates BitTorrent Chain (BTTC) — a layer-2 proof-of-stake cross-chain scaling and interoperability network bridging TRON, Ethereum, and BSC — along with the BTT token, the BTFS decentralized storage layer, and BitTorrent Speed. Its developer surface spans the local uTorrent Web UI API for controlling torrent clients and the BitTorrent Chain developer documentation for building on the BTTC network. Surfaced as a portfolio company of dcm-ventures and enriched into the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Nova Labs
providers.description: Nova Labs, Inc. is the company behind the Helium Network, a decentralized wireless network that replaces traditional carrier infrastructure with community-hosted Hotspots and is coordinated on the Solana blockchain and incentivized with the HNT token. Helium operates two networks: a global LoRaWAN network for low-power IoT devices and a cellular/Wi-Fi offload network for mobile connectivity (Helium Mobile). Nova Labs open-sources the network's protocol surface as gRPC/Protobuf service definitions (the helium/proto config, router, and proof-of-coverage services) and publishes a set of first-party client libraries, a command-line tool, and Rust crates for cryptography and protobuf types. This profile was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and enriched from Nova Labs' public developer surface; much of the legacy Helium IoT REST API tooling is archived following the network's migration to Solana.

providers.name: Hubble Protocol
providers.description: Hubble Protocol is a Solana-based decentralized finance (DeFi) protocol that lets users borrow the USDH stablecoin against multiple crypto collateral assets (SOL, mSOL, stSOL, ETH, BTC and more) with interest-free, fixed-fee loans held open for unlimited time. The protocol pairs a Stability Vault, a Peg Stability Module, a hybrid liquidation model, and native yield on deposited collateral. Developers integrate with Hubble on-chain through its Anchor programs (IDLs published on GitHub) and the open-source "@hubbleprotocol/hubble-sdk" TypeScript client, which exposes borrowing market states, HBB staking and USDH stability-pool data, user loans, treasury and circulating-supply metrics, and peg-stability swaps. Hubble published security audits (Arcadia, Kudelski, Smart State, Sec3) and runs a funded bug-bounty program; its core contributors later built Kamino Finance.

providers.name: DoubleZero
providers.description: DoubleZero is a decentralized physical infrastructure network (DePIN) that builds and operates a global, permissionless, dedicated-fiber backbone for distributed systems like blockchains — delivering low-latency, high-throughput connectivity where milliseconds matter. Its two-ring architecture pairs edge-node filtering with private high-bandwidth transport, connecting Solana validators, RPCs, and market-data consumers directly to one another. The network is coordinated by onchain smart contracts on Solana and powered by the 2Z SPL token, which meters bandwidth access, rewards fiber and device contributors for measured performance, and drives stake delegation. Operators connect through the first-party `doublezero` CLI and `doublezerod` daemon. Founded by Austin Federa with Malbec Labs; backed by Multicoin Capital and Dragonfly Capital.

providers.name: My AI
providers.description: My AI Inc. is the company behind Me Protocol, a universal open rewards infrastructure that lets brands issue, redeem, and swap loyalty rewards across a decentralized cross-brand ecosystem through a single API integration. Founded in 2022 by Robert Wesley and Paul Oamen and backed by 500 Global, the protocol combines an EVM smart-contract layer (Sepolia, Hedera, Base, Polygon), a hosted Platform-as-a-Service REST API, and embeddable SDKs — an AI agent chatbot widget plus drop-in React and inline payment components — so merchants can plug frictionless open rewards into web and agent-driven storefronts for the emerging AI Agent Economy.

providers.name: Figure Markets
providers.description: Figure Markets is a blockchain-native digital-asset marketplace built on the Provenance Blockchain that lets individuals and institutions trade, borrow against, and earn yield on crypto and real-world assets from a single account. Its exchange runs on Connamara's EP3 matching engine with FIX and REST APIs, offering a central limit order book for crypto (BTC, ETH, and more), equities, bonds, alternative assets, and YLDS, the first SEC-registered yielding stablecoin. Products include Figure Exchange (pro trading), crypto-backed loans, Democratized Prime (HELOC-backed yield), and self-custodied wallets, bridging traditional order-book finance with on-chain clearing and settlement. The company is backed by DCM Ventures. The trading API is served from api.figuremarkets.com and is access-controlled; no public OpenAPI is currently published.

providers.name: Instadapp
providers.description: Instadapp is a decentralized finance (DeFi) middleware company that scales DeFi for users and developers through non-custodial Smart Accounts. Its core DSA (DeFi Smart Accounts / DeFi Smart Layer) protocol aggregates lending, DEX, and yield protocols behind a single upgradable smart-contract layer, driven by a composable cast() function, with connectors and resolvers for protocols such as Aave, Compound, MakerDAO, and Uniswap. Instadapp also builds Fluid (a capital-efficient lending and DEX protocol), Avocado (a smart-contract wallet with account, gas, and smart-contract execution), and Instadapp Lite (simplified DeFi vaults). It supports Ethereum, Polygon, Optimism, Arbitrum, Base, Avalanche, BNB Chain, Fantom, Gnosis, Scroll, and Polygon zkEVM. The developer surface is on-chain smart contracts plus first-party JavaScript and TypeScript SDKs published to npm; there is no first-party REST API. Instadapp is backed by Pantera Capital.

providers.name: Mango Markets
providers.description: Mango Markets is a decentralized derivatives exchange and money market built on Solana, operated by the Blockworks Foundation. Mango v4 introduces unified margin accounts that combine spot trading, perpetual futures, and borrow/lend in a single risk engine, settled by the on-chain Mango v4 program. Beyond the on-chain program and the TypeScript client, the project exposes low-latency public market-data feeds through the mango-feeds geyser services - the Fills Feed (service-mango-fills, fills.mngo.cloud) and the Orderbook Feed (service-mango-orderbook, orderbook.mngo.cloud) - which stream fill events and L2/L3 orderbook state for Mango V4 Perp markets and Openbook spot markets over WebSocket.

providers.name: NATIX
providers.description: NATIX Network is a decentralized physical infrastructure (DePIN) network building what it calls the world's largest on-street camera network to power Physical AI, autonomous driving, and real-time mapping. Drivers use the Drive& smartphone app and the VX360 plug-and-earn smart camera for Tesla to collect, validate, anonymize, and monetize multi-camera dashcam footage, earning $NATIX token rewards. NATIX packages the resulting data into training datasets, edge cases, and OpenScenario/OpenDrive simulation scenarios for AI and mapping customers, and runs an on-chain token economy with staking, governance, and xNodes. As of 2026 it reports 2.89M+ registered drivers and coverage across 33 countries. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a Techstars portfolio company; enrichment confirms NATIX publishes no public REST/GraphQL developer API — the surface is consumer apps, an on-chain token, and a proprietary partner Vision SDK.

providers.name: April
providers.description: April (aPriori, apr.io) is a MEV-powered liquid staking protocol on the Monad blockchain. Users stake MON tokens through aPriori's self-custodial staking vault and receive aprMON, a reward-bearing liquid staking token that accrues proof-of-stake plus MEV yield and can be used across Monad DeFi while retaining full custody. The protocol also operates Swapr (a DEX aggregator), an order-flow segmentation and MEV infrastructure layer, and the $APR token with an APR Boost rewards program. aPriori is documented on GitBook with an introduction, a Monad testnet guide, a MON faucet guide, and a smart-contract integration reference; it is a smart-contract protocol rather than a keyed REST API. Surfaced into the API Evangelist network as a crypto portfolio lead.

providers.name: Baxus
providers.description: BAXUS is a peer-to-peer marketplace for buying, selling, trading, and storing fine and rare wine and spirits, built on the Solana blockchain. Founded in 2021 by Tzvi Wiesel and based in Woodland Park, New Jersey, BAXUS authenticates physical bottles and holds them in climate-controlled vaults, then tokenizes each as an NFT that serves as a digital certificate of ownership and provenance. Beyond the marketplace and Vault, BAXUS operates the BoozApp collection app, an open-source AI whiskey sommelier agent (BOB), and Whisky-Goggles AI bottle recognition. Its backend API at services.baxus.co powers bottle search, marketplace listings, and user bar collections. Backed by Multicoin Capital.

providers.name: Code4rena
providers.description: Code4rena (C4) is a competitive smart-contract security auditing platform that connects Web3/DeFi projects (sponsors) with a global community of security researchers (wardens) through time-boxed competitive audits and ongoing bug bounties. Sponsors fund an audit, wardens compete to surface vulnerabilities, and judges rate severity, validity, and quality to distribute awards via a ranked-curve incentive model. Over five years the platform ran 512+ audits, engaged 16,600+ researchers, and surfaced 26,898 findings including 1,607 high-severity vulnerabilities. Code4rena announced it is winding down operations, seeing active competitions and bounties through to completion. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as a paradigm portfolio company; the platform is web/app-based with GitBook documentation and does not publish a public REST/GraphQL API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Arc
providers.description: Arc is an intelligent cash management platform for technology companies that consolidates business banking, treasury, debt capital, and AI-powered financial services into a single dashboard. Customers can sweep idle cash into yield-bearing accounts, manage liquidity across multiple accounts, raise debt capital, and access AI tooling for financial operations. Arc also offers a Global Treasury product that lets qualifying startups invest in US Treasury Bills as non-US entities while safeguarding funds in US brokerage accounts. The platform is primarily delivered through a hosted web application rather than a public REST API, and integrations are coordinated through Arc's solutions and customer success teams. Arc is positioned as a unified financial operating system for venture-backed and growth-stage technology businesses.

providers.name: AstroPay
providers.description: AstroPay is a Uruguay-founded fintech and electronic money institution offering a multicurrency wallet, virtual and physical AstroCards, FX, and cross-border money transfers for consumers across Latin America, plus a business platform that lets merchants accept payments, issue cards, manage payroll, and pay out to wallets and bank accounts. AstroPay is regulated as an EMI in the UK, Denmark, Isle of Man, and Brazil, and operates the AstroPay wallet across Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Mexico, Peru, Colombia, Uruguay, and additional global corridors with support for ARS, BRL, CLP, COP, EUR, GBP, MXN, PEN, USD, USDT, and UYU. For developers, AstroPay exposes a comprehensive REST platform spanning payments, payouts, PIX instant payments in Brazil, issued cards, savings accounts, scheme transfers, user account management, tokenization (PCI-compliant card collection), settlements, transaction reporting, hosted and embedded Checkout, QR-code POS, Wallet-on-File account linking, Cashouts, and Webhooks — accessed through `developers.astropay.com` with HMAC-signed callbacks and an OAuth/API-key authentication model.

providers.name: Palm
providers.description: Palm is an AI cash flow forecasting platform for corporate treasury and finance teams. It sits above existing Treasury Management Systems (TMS) and ERPs, unifying visibility across cash positions and forecasting liquidity directly from bank and transaction data. Palm learns the timing and size of recurring cash flows from historical transactions to keep a rolling 13-week-and-longer forecast current automatically, and combines ERP data, bank transactions, and 25+ AI models to improve forecast accuracy by over 60%. The product spans AI cash forecasting, what-if scenario modeling, continuous forecast-vs-actual variance analysis, automated daily cash positioning across banks and currencies, surplus-cash investment identification, board-ready treasury reporting, and a "Pulse" anomaly-detection assistant. Palm is a speedinvest portfolio company. It integrates with TMS (Coupa, FIS, ION, Kyriba), banks (Citi, HSBC, J.P. Morgan), investment platforms, data warehouses, and ERPs (SAP, IFS), but does not publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Dework
providers.description: Dework is a Web3-native task-management and bounty platform for DAOs and decentralized teams. Organizations create bounties, projects, and task boards; contributors build an on-chain reputation profile, claim or apply to tasks, and get paid in the DAO's own token or stablecoins from supported wallets (Gnosis/Safe, MetaMask, Phantom, WalletConnect). Dework offers token- and Discord-role gating, two-way Discord and GitHub sync, Notion and Coordinape integrations, batch payments, reputation staking, roadmaps, and leaderboards. It aggregates bounties and grants from hundreds of DAOs. The app is backed by an Apollo GraphQL API at api.dework.xyz; product documentation lives on GitBook. Backed by Paradigm.

providers.name: OXIO
providers.description: OXIO is a Telecom-as-a-Service (TaaS) platform that lets brands, enterprises, and fintechs launch and operate their own branded mobile networks (MVNOs) through a single API, without building traditional telecom infrastructure. Its API-first platform unifies multiple carriers behind one integration and layers on no-code service creation (BrandVNO), AI-driven subscriber and network intelligence (BrandIQ), and multi-carrier connectivity (OXIO Network). Developers use OXIO's RESTful APIs and sandbox for programmatic line and subscription management, payments, fraud detection, and CRM/ERP synchronization. OXIO was surfaced as a portfolio company of Multicoin Capital (its GitHub org carries Stellar blockchain SDK forks) and enriched from its public web surface; the full developer documentation is gated behind authorized-customer access.

providers.name: Primodium Inc.
providers.description: Primodium Inc. (primodiumxyz) is a developer-focused studio building fully on-chain applications and games on Ethereum and Solana. It ships two on-chain games — Primodium, a space-based factory-building game, and Primodium: Empires, a turn-based prediction-market game — both built with MUD and Phaser, alongside a suite of open-source developer libraries and infrastructure: Reactive Tables (a strictly-typed reactive table library for MUD apps), a Solana DEX Indexer Stack exposing a GraphQL API over Hasura/Timescale, a tRPC transaction-sponsoring DEX server, an off-chain MUD indexer, and gasless-transaction relayers. All tooling is published open-source under the MIT license via the primodiumxyz GitHub organization and the @primodiumxyz npm scope.

providers.name: CoinMarketCap
providers.description: CoinMarketCap is the leading crypto market data and rankings platform. The CoinMarketCap Pro API exposes 40+ REST endpoints covering cryptocurrency listings, quotes, OHLCV, exchange data, DEX/on-chain data, derivatives, global metrics, Fear and Greed index, content, and tools. Most data refreshes every 1 minute. Authentication uses an X-CMC_PRO_API_KEY header.

providers.name: Staircase
providers.description: Staircase, Inc. operates the Elephant Protocol (elephant.xyz), a decentralized property-data network that aggregates and cryptographically verifies fragmented county property and address records into trusted, agent-consumable data. It publishes 500,000+ enriched property data points and an unusually agent-native developer surface: a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server (@elephant-xyz/mcp, both stdio and hosted), an Elephant CLI (@elephant-xyz/cli) for oracle data transformation and on-chain proof submission to Polygon, a fact-sheet generator, and a library of 14 published Agent Skills for county-data ingestion. An Enterprise API is offered to organizations at scale. Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners; originally a mortgage-technology API company, now focused on real estate data infrastructure.

providers.name: Cross River Bank
providers.description: Cross River Bank is an FDIC-insured chartered bank that operates as a sponsor bank and banking-as-a-service (BaaS) provider for fintech companies, embedded-finance platforms, and crypto / stablecoin issuers. The product surface is delivered through the Cross River Operating System (COS) - a proprietary API-driven banking core with real-time subledger generation - and includes accounts, ACH and Same-Day ACH, RTP and FedNow instant payments, wires, card issuing and processing (Visa / Mastercard), merchant acquiring, stablecoin rails, consumer and SMB lending, and capital markets / loan participation services. API access is gated behind a partner onboarding process; documentation and sandbox are at docs.crossriver.com.

providers.name: Mirror
providers.description: Mirror Protocol is a decentralized finance (DeFi) synthetic-assets protocol built on the Terra blockchain (with an Ethereum bridge) that mints mirrored assets (mAssets) tracking the prices of real-world equities, commodities, and other assets. Its public developer surface is the Mirror API — a read-only GraphQL data service exposing protocol state (assets, prices, positions, staking) — together with the mirror.js JavaScript/TypeScript SDK and the mirrorcli command-line interface for querying and executing against the on-chain CosmWasm contracts. The protocol is governed by the MIR token. It is now in a legacy/dormant state following the May 2022 Terra/LUNA collapse, though its documentation, GitHub org, SDKs, and GraphQL endpoint remain reachable.

providers.name: Moola
providers.description: Moola Market is a non-custodial, decentralized liquidity protocol on the Celo blockchain that democratizes access to yield and credit. Depositors earn compound interest that is paid by borrowers who take out over-collateralized loans, delegated loans, or flash loans. The protocol shares ancestry with the Aave v2 codebase, is open source and independently audited, and issues interest-bearing mTokens (mcUSD, mcEUR, mcREAL, mCELO) redeemable one-to-one for the underlying Celo stable assets. Moola is a smart-contract protocol rather than an HTTP API: developers integrate by calling on-chain contracts (deposit, withdraw, borrow, repay, flash loan) from a supported wallet. Backed by Polychain Capital.

providers.name: Asset Reality
providers.description: Asset Reality builds end-to-end software infrastructure for the seizure, management, custody, and disposal of both physical and virtual (crypto) assets, purpose-built for law enforcement, defense, and government agencies. Its platform unifies the asset-recovery lifecycle across four solutions — SEIZE, MANAGE, DEPLOY, and ESCROW — replacing clipboard-and-spreadsheet legacy processes with a single system that preserves asset value through investigation, confiscation, forfeiture, and reallocation to public purposes. The company is FCA-authorized to offer crypto custody in the UK, integrates with providers such as Fireblocks and Taxbit, and runs an Academy offering virtual-asset seizure certifications.

providers.name: GEODNET
providers.description: GEODNET (Global Earth Observation Decentralized Network) is a Web3/DePIN blockchain-based RTK (Real-Time Kinematics) GNSS correction network. It incentivizes operators to deploy permanent GNSS reference stations ("Satellite Miners") that broadcast real-time correction data, letting nearby devices achieve centimeter-level positioning accuracy. Station operators earn GEOD token rewards, with a target of 100,000 evenly distributed base stations worldwide — roughly twenty times larger than existing CORS networks. The correction data fuels robots, drones, autonomous vehicles, precision agriculture, construction, surveying, and consumer mapping. Developer-facing surfaces are the GEODNET Console web platform, the RTK coverage service, and DAO governance; the GEOD token spans Polygon and Solana. This profile was seeded as a Multicoin Capital portfolio lead and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Ithaca
providers.description: Ithaca is a crypto-infrastructure company (backed by Paradigm) building open-source developer tooling to accelerate the crypto frontier. Its flagship product, Porto, is a TypeScript SDK for passwordless authentication and payments on the web — letting applications and wallets create, manage, and interact with next-generation Ethereum accounts (keychains with passkeys, permissions, subscriptions, and native cross-chain interoperability) without passwords, extensions, seed phrases, or API keys. The stack also includes the Account smart contracts (Solidity), the Relay cross-chain transaction router and RPC server (Rust) for EIP-7702 accounts, and Odyssey, an experimental open-source Layer 2 testnet. The Ithaca team has since joined Tempo (tempo.xyz), and the Porto product is sunsetting on 2026-07-24 with users moving to porto.sh.

providers.name: MyCrypto
providers.description: MyCrypto is a free, open-source, client-side interface for managing Ethereum accounts and interacting with the Ethereum blockchain. Founded in 2015, it is a non-custodial wallet — private keys never leave the user's device — supporting hardware wallets, Web3 and browser wallets, and offline transaction signing. In February 2022 MyCrypto was acquired by ConsenSys to consolidate with MetaMask and unify the Web3 wallet experience. MyCrypto ships no public REST API; its developer surface is the open-source application codebase and the JavaScript/TypeScript libraries (eth-scan, ethereum-blockies-base64, asset mappings) published under the MyCryptoHQ GitHub organization.

providers.name: Cryptio
providers.description: Cryptio is an enterprise-grade crypto accounting, reporting, and audit platform that provides an institutional system of record for digital assets. It ingests and normalizes transaction data across 150+ blockchains, exchanges, custodians, and DeFi protocols, then automates sub-ledger accounting, cost-basis and gain/loss calculation, reconciliation, tokenization compliance, and loan management. Cryptio syncs into traditional ERP and accounting systems (NetSuite, Xero, QuickBooks, Dynamics 365, Oracle Fusion, SAP, Sage) and is used by 400+ institutions including exchanges, banks, asset managers, and DeFi enterprises to produce audit-ready financial reporting for digital assets.

providers.name: Trust Token
providers.description: TrustToken, founded in San Francisco in 2017 and rebranded as Archblock in November 2022, builds infrastructure for moving institutional funds and real-world assets onto blockchain rails. The company created the TrueUSD (TUSD) stablecoin and the TrueCurrencies family, and launched TrueFi, an on-chain under-collateralized lending protocol governed by the TRU token. Today Archblock operates a marketplace and fund-tokenization platform for institutional capital at app.archblock.com, with smart contracts, audits, and bug bounty programs published through its trusttoken GitHub organization. Backed by a16z, Founders Fund, BlockTower, and Morgan Creek.

providers.name: Deblock
providers.description: Deblock is a fintech company offering a hybrid financial app that combines a fully licensed current account with a French IBAN and a Visa debit card alongside a self-custodial (non-custodial) crypto wallet, so customers hold their own private keys while spending fiat and crypto in everyday life. Founded by former Revolut and Ledger team members and registered with France's AMF as a digital-asset service provider, Deblock lets users buy, sell and swap crypto through an integrated exchange, earn interest on their current account balance, and round spare change up into Bitcoin. Its consumer product is delivered as a mobile app under the tagline "Own Your Money"; Deblock does not currently publish a public developer API, portal, or documentation. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network from the Speedinvest venture portfolio.

providers.name: Romit
providers.description: Romit was a bank-agnostic digital wallet and payment-gateway platform for the card-not-present merchant-acquiring industry, built by a team of ex-Robocoin (bitcoin ATM) founders and backed by the 500 Global (500 Startups) accelerator. The Romit Merchant Suite let merchants stop chargebacks, reduce fraud and resolve disputes, while its consumer wallet let customers securely store payment methods, view transactions and communicate with merchants. Its OAuth2 REST API (api.romit.io/v1) exposed Banking (cards + linked bank accounts), Identity/KYC, Transfer (authorize/capture/refund/void money movement), Subscription, Plan and Invoice resources. Romit (romit.io) has since ceased operations; this profile captures the API surface derived from the surviving public evidence.

providers.name: Eden Network
providers.description: Eden Network is an Ethereum MEV, block-building, and orderflow infrastructure project (EDEN token, launched 2021, evolving from the earlier Archer DAO relay). It operated a gRPC mempool streaming service, an Eden block builder and reverse proxy (eden-geth / eden-proxy), subgraph-backed data tooling, and a DEX API for the Ethereum ecosystem. The original edennetwork.io web property has since lapsed; the canonical, still-live developer surface is the eden-network GitHub organization and the published npm and Go packages. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Multicoin Capital and enriched from those public sources.

providers.name: Forte
providers.description: Forte is a Web3 economic infrastructure company building compliance and economic tools for games and digital-asset economies. Its flagship product is the Forte Rules Engine, a free, open-source, EVM-compatible on-chain policy engine that lets smart-contract developers define composable, adaptive rules (KYC gates, OFAC/sanctions screening, vesting schedules, circuit breakers, and other economic guardrails) without hardcoding logic into their contracts. The Rules Engine ships a TypeScript SDK and Solidity client contracts, and is complemented by a ZK Policy Engine for privacy-preserving policy enforcement. Forte is backed by a16z, Canaan Partners, and Trinity Ventures.

providers.name: LifeSite
providers.description: LifeSite is a data protection and digital asset company that helps organizations safeguard sensitive information, simplify compliance, and digitally verify ownership. Its Vault product is an encrypted store for personally identifiable, financial, and health information used by both enterprises and families to organize and collaborate on vital documents. TokenX, its Web3 arm, tokenizes real-world assets — critical minerals, carbon credits, and sports and consumer goods — so provenance and ownership can be authenticated without blockchain expertise. A Wellness product covers health, testing, and vaccination tracking for enterprises and events, and a Platform offering exposes LifeSite's building blocks and APIs for partners building tailored data-management applications. LifeSite is sales-led: the Platform APIs are described publicly but no developer portal, API reference, or specification is published, and access is arranged through a demo request.

providers.name: Boardroom Governance
providers.description: Boardroom is a governance aggregation platform that helps developers fetch and display governance data across DAOs and decentralized networks. The Boardroom Governance API provides access to proposals, votes, protocols, and voter data for Web3 governance applications.

providers.name: Blockskye
providers.description: Blockskye is an enterprise travel management and payments platform for large corporate travel programs, founded in 2017 and headquartered in New York. It combines a consumer-grade online booking tool sourced through direct supplier and NDC connectivity, BMAX direct settlement that wires a customer's ERP straight to travel suppliers so booked travel bypasses corporate cards and expense reports, B360 for capturing personal co-brand card loyalty on business trips while holding policy compliance, and real-time reporting across every booking channel, with transactions recorded to a tamper-resistant distributed ledger. Blockskye delivers an end-to-end corporate travel solution in partnership with KAYAK for Business. The platform is sold and operated as an enterprise service: the booking, servicing and settlement application runs at horizon.blockskye.com behind a customer login and the knowledge base sits behind a Freshworks OAuth login. Blockskye operates a live production API host at api.blockskye.com but publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Fhenix
providers.description: Fhenix is a blockchain R&D company building confidential computing for EVM-compatible chains using Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE). Its CoFHE (FHE Coprocessor) lets Solidity smart contracts compute directly on encrypted data — encrypt inputs client-side, operate on ciphertexts on-chain via the FHE.sol Solidity libraries, and unseal results through a threshold decryption network, so sensitive state stays private without ever being decrypted on-chain. The developer stack is a smart-contract-plus-client-library surface (not a REST API): the cofhejs TypeScript SDK, Hardhat/Foundry plugins and starters, the fhenix-contracts Solidity libraries, and mock contracts for local testing. CoFHE is live on public testnets (Ethereum Sepolia, Arbitrum Sepolia, Base Sepolia) with mainnet planned. Fhenix is backed by Multicoin Capital.

providers.name: Milo Credit
providers.description: Milo (formerly Milo Credit) is a Miami-based financial technology company and licensed mortgage lender that pioneered crypto-backed lending. Milo lets cryptocurrency holders access cash or finance U.S. real estate without selling their digital assets, offering crypto-backed mortgages with up to 100% financing, self-custody mortgages, and crypto-backed loans funded in as little as 24 hours, with rates starting around 7%. The company was an early portfolio investment of QED Investors and operates as a consumer-facing lending platform rather than a developer/API-first company. As of this enrichment pass Milo publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or API documentation; its public surface is a consumer web application (app.milo.io), a marketing site, a blog, an FAQ, and a hosted trust/security center. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record.

providers.name: Arf
providers.description: Arf is a Switzerland-regulated liquidity and settlement platform for cross-border payments, providing short-term, receivable-backed, revolving working capital to licensed payment institutions and money-transfer operators. Its core product, Arf Liquidity, lets payment companies settle across any corridor 24/7 without prefunding destination accounts, using regulated real-world-asset-backed digital assets and stablecoins (including USDC) for native on-ramp/off-ramp value transfer and real-time treasury management. Arf is a compliance-first, VQF self-regulatory-organization member serving only licensed financial institutions, and partners with Circle, Stellar, and Visa. This profile was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and enriched from Arf's public web presence; Arf does not currently publish a public developer portal or API.

providers.name: PiggyVest
providers.description: PiggyVest is a Lagos-based Nigerian fintech (operated by Piggytech Global Limited, RC 1405222) running the country's largest online savings and investment platform, with 6M+ registered users as of 2026. Founded in January 2016 by Somto Ifezue, Odunayo Eweniyi, and Joshua Chibueze as Piggybank.ng and rebranded to PiggyVest in April 2019, the company digitizes the traditional Nigerian "kolo" piggy-bank, layering automated savings, fixed-term safe-locks, naira and dollar wallets, and curated investments on top of licensed banking partners (originally United Bank for Africa) and a PCI-DSS-compliant payment stack. The consumer product family includes Piggybank (automated daily/weekly/monthly savings), SafeLock (fixed-tenor savings with up-front interest), Target Savings (goal-based saving, solo or group), Flex Naira (flexible wallet with free transfers), Flex Dollar / SafeLock Dollar (USD savings), HouseMoney (rent wallet), Investify (curated investment opportunities), GetIT (lifestyle purchase plans), Piggy Points (rewards), and an Accountability Partner feature, all delivered through iOS, Android, and web apps published by Piggytech Global. On the developer side, PiggyVest operates a separate B2B brand — PiggyVest Business — at piggyvest.business and exposes the PiggyVest Business API at api.piggyvest.business, documented at www.piggyvestbusiness.com/docs. The Business API is a Bearer-token authenticated REST API (secret key in Authorization header) covering customer creation and retrieval, customer wallets (create / retrieve / list, accrued-interest tracking, reserved account numbers, funding accounts), wallet-to-wallet and bank transfers (with name inquiry and bank lookup), transactions (status, history, T+1 settlement), scheduled payments (create / cancel / reactivate), webhooks for real-time event notifications, and a "Pay with Pocket" SDK / hosted-checkout integration that lets merchants accept payments funded from a Piggyvest user's Pocket balance. Default rate limits are approximately 100 requests per minute. No public OpenAPI specification, official SDK packages, or open-source client libraries are currently published; access is gated by signing up for a PiggyVest Business dashboard account. Alongside the API, PiggyVest Business offers Invoicing, Customizable Accounts, Business Safelock, Investify for Business, and business savings earning up to 18% per annum. Public engineering presence is limited — the Piggytech Global GitHub org (github.com/PiggyTech) hosts a small set of community wrappers (react-paystack, Smile Identity Node.js and React Native wrappers) and the consumer brand maintains a static piggyvest.github.io site, but there is no developer org publishing official Piggyvest Business SDKs.

providers.name: PsyOptions
providers.description: PsyOptions is a decentralized options protocol built on Solana by Mithraic Labs, providing on-chain American-style options contracts originally designed for use with the Serum/OpenBook DEX. Rather than a hosted REST API, it exposes its functionality through open-source on-chain Anchor/BPF programs and first-party TypeScript client libraries (the @mithraic-labs npm scope: psy-american, psyoptions, market-meta, psy-token-registry, psy-metrics) plus a Rust crate. The project has since been sunset: its documentation and marketing sites are shut down, though the GitHub repositories and published packages remain available for reference. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Pantera Capital. Sector: crypto / DeFi.

providers.name: Silo Finance
providers.description: Silo Finance is a decentralized, non-custodial lending protocol built around isolated money markets. Each market pairs a single collateral asset with a borrowable asset in its own risk silo, so the failure or manipulation of one asset cannot cascade into unrelated markets — the isolation model that distinguishes Silo from pooled lenders. The protocol is delivered as onchain smart contracts (Silo V1, V2 and V3) deployed across Ethereum and other EVM chains, with an application at silo.finance, developer and protocol-architecture documentation at docs.silo.finance, third-party security audits, and an open GitHub organization publishing the contracts, subgraph and indexer. Silo Finance is backed by Electric Capital and is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a DeFi lending provider.

providers.name: Exa Finance
providers.description: EXA Finance is a French Web3 company, founded in 2021, that builds EXA Market — a peer-to-peer NFT and multi-asset marketplace on the Algorand blockchain. Because Algorand represents both fungible tokens and NFTs under the single ASA (Algorand Standard Asset) standard, the EXA Market protocol lets users bundle up to four assets into a "basket" and trade them in a single transaction, sell NFTs for any ASA rather than only the native ALGO token, make peer-to-peer offers, and run standard sales, normal and Dutch/reverse auctions, and multi-mints. Creators set an on-chain royalty fee of up to 15% globally against their creator address, payable in ALGO, USDC, USDT and other opted-in assets. The protocol is governed by the EXA token (ASA ID 1888888888) through the EXA Community DAO, whose EXRC/EXIP proposal lifecycle is modeled on Uniswap, dYdX, Tinyman and Blur. EXA raised a $2M seed round in January 2022 with Speedinvest, Lemniscap, Big Brain Holdings, Borderless Capital, Encode Club, Meld Ventures, 11-11 DG Partners and 0x Ventures. EXA Market publishes no public HTTP/REST API: its programmable surface is on-chain Algorand smart contracts (listing, offer and auction contracts, published as TEAL approval programs), reached through standard Algorand algod and indexer node APIs and the Algorand SDKs.

providers.name: Structure
providers.description: Structure (Structure Financial Inc.) is a Web3 platform for designing, backtesting, and deploying fully automated, permissionless crypto trading strategies without writing code. Its visual strategy editor and AI-assisted code generation let users build algorithmic strategies that compile to Rust and deploy non-custodially to decentralized exchanges including Hyperliquid, Drift, and Jupiter; strategies receive trading-only permissions so funds never leave the user's vault. The company documents live, paper, and backtest execution paths and references MCP-agent and code-based access alongside its no-code visual interface. Founded by MIT and Jump Trading alumni and backed by the investors behind Coinbase and Solana.

providers.name: Upstream
providers.description: Upstream is a no-code, full-stack platform for launching and operating DAOs (decentralized autonomous organizations), letting communities create a DAO with a Gnosis multi-signature wallet, DAO contract, and vote delegation contract without technical experience. The platform blends on-chain smart contracts (built on OpenZeppelin, audited by Upshield) with off-chain forums, proposals, polls, and events, and maintains the open-source Fortuna service that indexes ERC20/ERC721/ERC1155 transfer events on Ethereum. Upstream is backed by Bloomberg Beta. The company does not currently publish a public developer API; its backend at api.upstreamapp.com is undocumented and product documentation lives at guide.upstreamapp.com.

providers.name: Orchid Labs
providers.description: Orchid Labs is the company behind Orchid, an open-source, decentralized marketplace for bandwidth and a privacy-focused VPN. Orchid lets users pay for VPN service through nanopayments settled on a probabilistic payment layer built on Ethereum, using the OXT utility token and Orchid Accounts rather than traditional subscriptions. The stack includes an open-source multi-hop VPN client (Dart), the Orchid DApp for account creation and management, a decentralized directory of bandwidth providers running as smart contracts, and an L2/L3 nanopayment protocol. Backed by a16z, Sequoia Capital, DFJ, and Polychain, Orchid Labs focuses on decentralized privacy infrastructure rather than a conventional developer REST API.

providers.name: Pump.fun
providers.description: Pump.fun is a Solana-based memecoin launchpad and livestreaming platform that lets anyone deploy a token with a bonding-curve market in seconds; tokens that reach a target market cap graduate to PumpSwap, the project's own AMM. The project does not publish a formally documented public REST API - the canonical integration surface is the on-chain Solana programs for token creation, bonding-curve trades, and PumpSwap liquidity, plus the open-source pump-fun-sdk client. Most "Pump.fun APIs" used in the wider ecosystem are third-party indexers (Bitquery, Helius, Jupiter, Tatum) wrapping that on-chain activity.

providers.name: Tranched
providers.description: Tranched is a London-based fintech building an embedded, on-chain securitisation platform that connects fintech lenders and loan originators directly to professional investors. Its "Deep Tokenisation" approach represents loans as on-chain tokens governed by Smart Loan Agreements and automated waterfall contracts, letting originators structure and launch institutional-grade asset-based financing transactions up to 90% faster and at lower cost than traditional securitisation, with automated compliance, reporting, and monitoring. Tranched connects to a lender's loan management system via API integration to retrieve the data required for assigning and monitoring loans. Founded in 2023 by Clement Larrue and Michael Elalouf, the company raised a $3.4M pre-seed round led by Speedinvest in November 2024.

providers.name: Rialo
providers.description: Rialo is an early-stage Layer 1 blockchain building high-throughput infrastructure with configurable privacy for real-world finance and the emerging agent economy. Developed by Subzero Labs and backed by Pantera Capital, Rialo positions itself as the infrastructure for the next generation of intelligent systems, replacing the fragile stack of off-chain automation with native, event-driven execution. Its architecture spans several first-class capabilities: the Rialo Omni Account (one account that transacts across multiple networks), Rialo Interop (native, fast, cheap cross-chain interoperability), Rialo IPC (Identity, Privacy, and Compliance built in), Rialo Stream (native data feeds for DeFi and real-world assets), and an event-driven Execution Engine supporting reactive transactions and conditional automation. The project is pre-mainnet; its developer surface consists of a dev portal, gated technical documentation, an interactive playground, a Learn hub of technical demos, and an active engineering blog.

providers.name: The Block
providers.description: The Block is a New York-based digital-assets research, analysis, and news brand founded in 2018, covering cryptocurrency, blockchain, and Web3 markets. Its subscription platform, The Block Pro, packages breaking news, in-depth research, proprietary datasets, and venture-funding intelligence for professional investors, funds, and enterprises. The Block Pro also exposes a set of license-gated APIs - a real-time News API (REST, request-only, JSON), a Deals/Funding API, an Ecosystems/Data API, and a WebSocket news stream - available only to organizations holding a Block Pro subscription. The APIs have no public developer portal or OpenAPI definition; access and technical documentation are arranged through The Block's client-services team.

providers.name: Voatz
providers.description: Voatz is a remote voting technology company providing secure, mobile-based voting for public elections and organizational governance. Voters cast ballots from a smartphone, tablet, or web browser, with identity assured through hardware-backed authentication and biometric verification, ballots anchored to a permissioned blockchain, and a voter-verifiable paper audit trail produced for every vote. The platform pairs the voter-facing mobile app with an administrative dashboard for election officials and supports accessibility features for voters with disabilities. Voatz has run elections across seven countries for more than five million voters, with pilots and deployments for U.S. counties (West Virginia, Utah County, Denver), political parties, and international election authorities. The company is a Techstars-backed startup. Voatz publishes no public developer API; its surface is a security, audit, and disclosure program rather than an integration platform.

providers.name: Argent
providers.description: Argent (rebranded to Ready, ready.co, in 2025) is a self-custodial smart-contract wallet company focused on Starknet and Ethereum. It builds account-abstraction wallets - the Ready / Argent X browser extension and mobile app, a seedless email and password Web Wallet, and a multisig - plus the open-source developer tooling dapps use to integrate them: the starknetkit connection SDK, session keys (@argent/x-sessions), multicall batching, get-starknet, and the Swift starknet.swift and web3.swift libraries. Argent ships no first-party REST API; integration is via these client SDKs and on-chain smart contracts, with developer documentation hosted at docs.ready.co. Surfaced as an index-ventures portfolio company and enriched here.

providers.name: TipLink
providers.description: TipLink is a Solana wallet-link platform that lets anyone create a shareable link or QR code holding crypto or an NFT, so a recipient can claim digital assets without first setting up a wallet. It ships as first-party TypeScript/JavaScript SDKs (notably @tiplink/api) and Solana Wallet Adapter UI components rather than a hosted REST API, and is used for airdrops, tipping, payments, and onboarding new users to Solana. Backed by Multicoin Capital.

providers.name: Bitmain
providers.description: Bitmain Technologies is a Beijing-based designer and manufacturer of ASIC cryptocurrency-mining hardware, best known for its Antminer line of Bitcoin (SHA-256) and other proof-of-work miners. Bitmain also operates Antpool, one of the world's largest Bitcoin mining pools, which exposes a public HTTP API that lets account operators programmatically read account balances, account and worker hashrate, worker lists, payment history, and pool-wide statistics. The Antpool API authenticates each request with an HMAC-SHA256 signature computed from the operator's user id, API key, and an incrementing nonce, and rate-limits clients to 600 requests per 10 minutes per IP. This company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Hongshan and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: PartyDAO
providers.description: PartyDAO is the decentralized autonomous organization behind Party Protocol, an open, GPL-3.0 protocol for on-chain group coordination that aims to make Ethereum "multiplayer." Party Protocol lets groups form a Party (a shared Ethereum account with members, an inventory, and governance), collectively crowdfund to acquire assets, govern shared holdings, and distribute value to members — all through audited Solidity smart contracts rather than a hosted HTTP API. PartyDAO also ships Party (party.app), a consumer application built on the protocol. The developer surface is entirely on-chain: smart contracts, deployed contract addresses, and technical documentation for integrating via web3 libraries and direct contract calls. There is no REST/HTTP API, hosted SDK, or OAuth surface; integration happens by calling the deployed contracts.

providers.name: Sumer
providers.description: Sumer (Sumer.Money) is a blockchain liquidity infrastructure protocol positioning itself as the most capital-efficient way to put crypto assets to work across chains. Users deposit native assets such as liquid staked ETH, and Sumer's correlation-aware risk engine matches assets and liabilities to mint synthetic suTokens (suETH, suUSD) that act as "money multipliers" — travelling across connected blockchains as collateral while the underlying deposit keeps accruing staking rewards and lending interest. The protocol runs an omnichain lending/borrowing market, a points and veSumer staking program, and its Supernova EVM chain, drawing price data from Chainlink, Pyth, RedStone, and Supra oracles. Backed by Pantera Capital and other crypto investors, with contracts audited by Certik, Ancilia, Tikkala, and CD Security.

providers.name: Cypherium
providers.description: Cypherium is a permissionless Layer-1 blockchain built to bridge centralized (CeFi) and decentralized (DeFi) finance and bring real-world assets on-chain at scale. It runs CypherBFT, a hybrid consensus that pairs GPU proof-of-work committee election with HotStuff Byzantine Fault Tolerance for near-instant finality, and is EVM/Solidity compatible (EVM chain ID 16166). Products include CypherLink (cross-ledger notary), Cypherium Connect (bank integration plugin, marketed as ISO 20022 compliant), the Cypherium Validator, and Cypherium ID (decentralized identity). Developers integrate through an Ethereum-style JSON-RPC node API (eth/web3/net/ personal/miner/txpool/admin namespaces over HTTP, WS and IPC) and a Coinbase Rosetta API implementation for exchange and wallet integration. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Pantera Capital and enriched into the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Fab.com
providers.description: Fab.com is a digital content marketplace operated by Epic Games, where creators buy and sell 3D models, materials, environments, VFX, audio, and game-ready assets. Launched in October 2024, Fab consolidated four of Epic's prior storefronts — the Unreal Engine Marketplace, the Sketchfab Store, Quixel, and the ArtStation Marketplace — into a single catalog with unified licensing, and integrates into Unreal Engine, UEFN, and the Epic Games Launcher. The fabcom entry was originally added to the API Evangelist network as an a16z portfolio lead for the earlier, unrelated Fab.com flash-sale design-commerce company (2011–2015), which wound down before the domain passed to Epic Games; see x-identity-note. Fab publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable specification as of this pass — the surface captured here is its documentation, support, and security-disclosure posture.

providers.name: Zilch
providers.description: Zilch is a London-headquartered "buy now, pay later" and ad-subsidised payments network founded in 2018, and one of the United Kingdom's most prominent BNPL brands. Rather than integrating at each retailer's checkout, Zilch is deliberately merchant-agnostic: consumers apply in the Zilch mobile app, receive a virtual (and physical) Mastercard, and can Pay-in-3, pay over six weeks, or Pay-now-and-earn-cashback anywhere Mastercard is accepted, online or in-store, through Apple Pay and Google Pay wallets. Because Zilch reaches merchants over the open Mastercard card rails and relies on partners such as Mastercard for card issuing and Checkout.com as its payments processor, it does not operate a public merchant-integration or developer platform the way a PSP or open-banking provider does. As of this review Zilch publishes no developer portal, no API reference, and no downloadable OpenAPI/Swagger specification; its public surface is a consumer marketing site, a help centre, and a customer sign-up/login app. This profile therefore records Zilch's verified public web properties honestly and carries no API entries, because none are publicly documented.

providers.name: Lootex
providers.description: Lootex is a Web3 infrastructure and AI application development company with eight years in the blockchain space, backed by 500 Global. It built a multi-chain NFT marketplace (Seaport protocol with aggregator support), the Lootex Studio minting tool, the Biru social platform, and Lootex Plus (an API and SDK offering to mint, trade, and integrate NFTs into apps and games). Its core marketplace infrastructure — a NestJS backend and Next.js frontend with blockchain event indexing and Web3 wallet authentication — is published as open source under Apache-2.0. Lootex is now sunsetting its consumer products (marketplace, Studio, and Biru wind down on 2026-04-04; assets stay in users' own non-custodial wallets) and pivoting to full-stack AI/Web3 development partnerships and open-source contributions.

providers.name: Brevis
providers.description: Brevis is a highly efficient ZK coprocessor and zkVM that empowers smart contracts to read from the full historical on-chain data across all supported blockchains and run customizable computations in a completely trust-free way. Developers build application circuits with the Brevis SDK (available in Go and TypeScript), implementing a Data Access Module to specify the historical blockchain data needed, an App Circuit for the computation logic, and an App Contract to receive ZK-verified or coChain-verified results on-chain. Brevis also operates ProverNet, an open marketplace for zero-knowledge proofs, and Pico, an open-source high-performance zkVM. Backed by Polychain.

providers.name: InvestaX
providers.description: InvestaX is a Singapore-based, MAS-licensed tokenization platform for real-world assets (RWAs), operated by IC SG Pte. Ltd. under a Capital Markets Services license (CMS100635) and a Recognised Market Operator license from the Monetary Authority of Singapore. The platform provides end-to-end infrastructure for the issuance, distribution, secondary trading, and custody of security tokens and tokenized securities, plus a Tokenization SaaS product for institutional issuers and RWA investment products such as tokenized money market funds and private credit. It supports multiple blockchain protocols including Ethereum, Polygon, BASE, Algorand, Tezos, and Hedera. Backed by 500 Global.

providers.name: Parallel Universe
providers.description: Parallel Universe Inc. (Parallel Studios) is the Toronto-based game studio behind Parallel, a free-to-play sci-fi trading card game, and the broader Parallel Universe franchise that includes Colony, an AI agent simulation game, and Sanctuary, a third-person extraction shooter. The studio anchors the Echelon Prime web3 gaming ecosystem, where players truly own their cards and in-game items as blockchain assets and the PRIME token powers governance and rewards. Backed by a16z (Andreessen Horowitz) and Paradigm, Parallel is a consumer game franchise distributed via the web, Epic Games, Steam, the Apple App Store, and Google Play. It publishes no public developer / REST API surface today; this profile captures the studio's public web, community, and legal properties as harvested by the API Evangelist enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Thruster
providers.description: Thruster was a yield-first decentralized exchange (DEX) built natively on the Blast Ethereum Layer 2, offering Uniswap-style v2 and v3 concentrated liquidity AMMs, a stableswap AMM, and a token launchpad. Backed by Pantera Capital, the protocol shut down on July 29, 2025 after completing THRUST holder redemptions; its thruster.finance website is offline, while the GitBook documentation and the ThrusterX GitHub organization (Solidity contracts and audit reports) remain the surviving public record. No REST/HTTP API was published; the developer surface was on-chain smart contracts on Blast.

providers.name: Azura
providers.description: Azura is an onchain trading platform that lets users trade any onchain asset priced in USD without managing wallets, bridging assets, or paying gas fees. Under the tagline "If it's onchain, it's on Azura," the app offers cross-chain token swaps across multiple blockchains in a single transaction, spot trading with multiple order types, token discovery and analysis, portfolio and PnL tracking, a referral system, and an Azurite rewards program, all with zero platform trading fees. Smart-contract interactions are algorithmically security-audited. Azura is a consumer-facing DeFi product (web app at app.azura.xyz) backed by Initialized Capital; it publishes user documentation and a blog but does not currently expose a public developer API, SDK, or specification surface.

providers.name: Enosys Markets
providers.description: Ēnosys (formerly Flare Finance) is a decentralized finance (DeFi) platform building on the Flare and Songbird networks. Its product suite spans DEX V2 and V3 automated market makers with liquidity provision, collateralized Loans, yield Farms with a token launchpad, a cross-chain Bridge, DeFi price Oracles built on the Flare Time Series Oracle (FTSO), the Skopos blockchain indexer, Oryy multi-signature self-custody vaults, and an NFT suite (Gallery, Ermis, Clover). Enosys interfaces are smart-contract based rather than a conventional REST API; developer integration happens through published Solidity contracts, subgraphs, and price-feed connectors in the flrfinance GitHub organization.

providers.name: UXD Protocol
providers.description: UXD Protocol is a decentralized stablecoin protocol built on Solana, operated by Soteria FZCO, whose UXD token is backed 100% by an Asset Liability Management Module that deploys collateral into delta-neutral positions, on-chain lending, and real-world assets. The protocol is governed by the UXP token, is documented on GitBook, publishes six third-party security audits and a self-run bug bounty, and ships an open-source Solana program with a TypeScript client on npm and a Rust CPI client on crates.io. Backed by Multicoin Capital.

providers.name: Web3Auth
providers.description: Web3Auth (now MetaMask Embedded Wallets) is a non-custodial threshold-key wallet and authentication platform. It provides client SDKs (Web, React, Vue, iOS, Android, Flutter, React Native, Unity, Unreal, Node.js) and a backend Auth Network for OAuth-anchored MPC key shares. Public HTTP surface is limited and SDK-first.

providers.name: Abra
providers.description: Abra is a digital asset wealth and treasury management platform founded in 2014 that provides institutional-grade services for high-net-worth individuals, institutions, corporations, and family offices across all 50 US states. Its products include Vault (segregated-account custody built on Fireblocks MPC wallet technology), proprietary Yield strategies on BTC, ETH, SOL and stablecoins, crypto-backed loans up to 50% LTV, and institutional treasury management, OTC execution, staking, and advisory. The company reports $10B+ in transaction volume and $2.5B+ in loans processed, and is backed by Pantera Capital. Abra does not currently publish a public developer API, API documentation, or SDK surface; this profile captures its public identity and probed domain security.

providers.name: Genopets
providers.description: Genopets is a free-to-play, move-to-earn NFT game built on the Solana blockchain that gamifies an active lifestyle. Players nurture a digital pet — a Genopet — that evolves from real-world physical activity tracked via step counting, then battle, craft, stake, and trade in-game NFTs and Habitats. The economy pairs the GENE governance token with the in-game KI utility token earned by moving. Genopets is developed by a studio backed by Pantera Capital and operates a consumer mobile/web game rather than a public developer API; no OpenAPI, SDK, or developer portal was found during enrichment.

providers.name: MonkeyTilt
providers.description: MonkeyTilt is a crypto-native online casino and sportsbook where players deposit, wager, and cash out in cryptocurrency across slots, table games, live dealer, and sports betting. The platform rewards play with points, prize drops, and the Tilt Club VIP program (bonuses and merch drops), and is backed by Pantera Capital. MonkeyTilt is a consumer gaming product: it runs an internal application API (disallowed to crawlers in robots.txt) but publishes no public developer program, API documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable API specifications as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Lore
providers.description: Lore is a multichain wallet for groups to win together, a co-ownership platform that lets collectives launch shared, multi-signature Safe wallets across Solana, Ethereum, Base, Blast, and Arbitrum. Its Co-Ownership Framework is an equity-tracking system over shared Vaults that lets a group start small and grow both assets and members over time, using Proposals, Group Deposits, Exits, Distributions, and Valuations to manage on-chain treasuries and investment clubs together. Lore provides a consumer application and documentation but does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or OpenAPI surface.

providers.name: Pontem
providers.description: Pontem is a Web3 product development studio building with the Move language on Aptos and other Layer 1 blockchains, in partnership with Aptos Labs. Its product portfolio spans the Pontem Wallet (a browser-extension and mobile crypto wallet for APT, MOVE, ETH, SOL and more), the Liquidswap decentralized exchange and AMM, the Lumio L2 VM-abstraction framework, and a Move developer tooling suite that includes the Move Code Playground, the IntelliJ Move IDE plugin, the ByteBabel Solidity-to-Move bytecode translator, and the Dove Move package manager. Pontem publishes first-party TypeScript SDKs, an embeddable Liquidswap web-component widget, wallet adapters, and CLIs. Backed by Pantera Capital, Animoca Brands, and Aptos Labs.

providers.name: Rain Financial
providers.description: Rain is a Middle East and North Africa (MENA) cryptocurrency exchange and digital-asset platform, operated through Rain Financial Inc. and its Bahrain entity Rain Management W.L.L. Founded in 2017 by Abdullah Almoaiqel, AJ Nelson, Joseph Dallago, and Yehia Badawy, Rain became the first crypto-asset company accepted into the Central Bank of Bahrain (CBB) regulatory sandbox and, in 2019, the first CBB-licensed crypto-asset service provider in the region. Rain Trading Limited later received approval from Abu Dhabi Global Market's Financial Services Regulatory Authority (FSRA) to expand across the UAE. Rain lets retail and institutional customers buy, sell, store, and manage Bitcoin, Ethereum, and other cryptocurrencies against multiple fiat currencies, with a Rain Pro offering for advanced traders and the majority of customer assets held in multi-signature cold storage. The company raised seed, Series A, and a $110M Series B (Paradigm, Kleiner Perkins), and is a portfolio company of 500 Global.

providers.name: iTrustCapital
providers.description: iTrustCapital (legal entity ITC2.0, Inc.) is a US fintech software platform for alternative assets, offering 24/7 self-directed access to dozens of cryptocurrencies and physical precious metals through three account types: tax-advantaged self-directed Crypto IRAs for retirement savings, Premium Custody Accounts (PCA) for everyday non-retirement investing, and Treasury Accounts for businesses, trusts, non-profits and other entities. The platform charges a 1% cryptocurrency transaction fee with no monthly, annual, startup, exit, storage or transfer fees, and runs a closed-loop system backed by third-party US banks, custodians (iTrust Custodial Services, Fortis Bank) and institutional storage providers. iTrustCapital is not an exchange, custodian, trust company, broker-dealer or investment adviser; all transactions on the platform are self-directed. As of this profiling pass the company publishes NO public developer API — its own help center states that it "does not offer any API integration to any third-party applications, including self-trading bots and coin trackers." Access is via the web app and the iOS/Android mobile apps only.

providers.name: Eunice
providers.description: Eunice is a London-based AI fintech building institutional-grade due diligence and monitoring infrastructure for digital assets and private markets. Its platform automates token due diligence, classification, risk analysis, and disclosure requirements — including an AI-powered MiCA whitepaper library for streamlining compliance with the EU's Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation — and delivers insights through a dashboard and API to exchanges, funds, custodians, issuers, and regulators. Founded in 2021 by Yi Luo, a second-time fintech entrepreneur and former VC, Eunice raised $8M in combined Seed and Pre-Seed funding led by Moonfire Ventures and Speedinvest with participation from Openspace Ventures in 2026, and counts Coinbase, Crypto.com, Copper, and Zodia Custody among its clients.

providers.name: Stader Labs
providers.description: Stader Labs is a non-custodial, smart-contract-driven liquid staking platform for Proof-of-Stake networks. It lets retail users, exchanges, and custodians stake crypto and receive tokenized liquid staking tokens (ETHx, MaticX, BNBx, NEARx and others) that stay usable across 40+ DeFi protocols while earning auto-compounding rewards, with no lock-up and no minimum stake. Stader operates as multi-chain middleware infrastructure across Ethereum, Polygon, BNB Chain, Hedera, Fantom, and NEAR, and its contracts have been audited by Sigma Prime, Halborn, Peckshield, Code4rena, and OtterSec.
